comment_evidence.clause: and those limited options have been given to you for a very specific reason—When you're creating a simple diorama and the designers have already put together a palette of gorgeous elements that fit the theme/season/lighting
comment_evidence.full_review:
Delightful marvel of a game that's put all of its focus into cozy vibes and low-impact moments of creative discovery. 
Starting with the concept of a sandbox with no goals, stakes or failure modes means 100% of the gameplay gets focuses on creation, discovery and exploration. When I say exploration, I don't mean traveling to new lands, but rather, "What happens when I drag a path over a steep rocky cliff, oh it becomes a carved stone staircase" or "If I put a building on stilts and pull its rooftop down to be a flat surface, could I create a raised wraparound deck?" 
The art design is incredible and is made even more astounding by the support it gets from the game's engine. Every lamp you place and every fence you construct is accompanied by fluid stop-motion-esque animations—even the Undo command animates the reversed effect.  
The player controls are almost ridiculously simple, and they highlight the incredible building engine that has gotten this game nominated for awards: I drag  this door away from ground level and it becomes a window, I add a second window beside it and it becomes a double window with shutters, I click that double window and its flowerbox becomes a clothesline connecting to the window on the neighboring building. It's really special to play around with, and it constantly feeds you creative fuel and ideas for your next cozy addition. 
I've seen some comments expressing unhappiness with the limited object options (only one type of fence, only one type of tree/flowerbed/etc) but I found that there is a TON you can do by manipulating the options you're given and by using them in different contexts, and those limited options have been given to you for a very specific reason—When you're creating a simple diorama and the designers have already put together a palette of gorgeous elements that fit the theme/season/lighting, it leaves you with the perfect tools to create your own happy place brick by brick. 
It's not a wildly addictive game that I'll play for 60 hours in my first week. But it's one I'll be glad to have in my library every time I need a quiet couple of hours in a Tiny Glade.

comment_evidence.clause: The limited options from the customization menu just made it feel repetitive
comment_evidence.full_review:
[b] Love it but it needs more! [/b]

[i] Why do I love it? [/i]

Honestly, this is one of the unique cozy games I have ever played. The graphics is so beautiful and satisfying. No pressure whatsoever, you just need to unleash your creativity! The 3D model, the cute animation and the design are top-tier - the reason why I bought it on the release date.

[i] What it lacks? [/i]

I played it for a couple of weeks and at first it was refreshing but as you go on, it was the same thing over and over again. The limited options from the customization menu just made it feel repetitive. What I'm pertaining to exactly is the unchangeable aspects like: just 1 design for grass/bushes/flowers/trees, No cute things and stuff like windmills/farm things/etc., the same pattern of walls/bricks/roof (just different colors) - you get my point.

[i] What do I suggest? [/i]

This game would be massive if - there are more varieties and you can mix and match season components. It's better if you don't have to choose a season/theme, you can start from scratch and with options to add stuff from other themes.

I know this game just recently got released but there's really a huge potential!

comment_evidence.clause: The clean milestone interface makes it easy to manage your next goal and gives you baby steps upgrading each piece just enough to make you think without overloading you with some Pacaso puzzle piece
comment_evidence.full_review:
Like a crackhead, I am easily captivated by this automation games. The original Shapez was a solid problem-solving itch that I like to scratch. In my mind, it was hard to top it. As they say in movies, the sequel is never as good as the original.  
Thankfully, Shapez 2 does not fall into that statistic. Despite being in early access the game works seamlessly and did not crash once in 50 hours on the highest graphics setting, suck it Cyberpunk.  
Of course they took the graphics to even greater heights making the original look like it was made on MS paint by highschoolers. Jumping from 2D to 3D is always the better choice unless you are trying to sell phone games. 
The clean milestone interface makes it easy to manage your next goal and gives you baby steps upgrading each piece just enough to make you think without overloading you with some Pacaso puzzle piece.  
 
Long story short, this is the third best automation games I’ve ever played... right behind Factorio and Satifactory. Be happy with 3rd place, Shapez 2.

comment_evidence.clause: The downsides include a clunky UI with only limited keybinding control and slow
comment_evidence.full_review:
This game satisfied my builder/creator itch nicely from the first screen to the last. The operator certification system is well designed to introduce complexity and solutions at a satisfactory pace, never letting you feel like you have nothing to do or no way to do it. Once you graduate to working with full belts (all 3 layers) you really feel like you're building factories, not just prototype designs. Do not ignore the milestone research points you earn after completing a milestone; however, it is worth it to only run up the level once you have a full belt solution, doubled if possible. Trains and the train launcher make it all possible and I'd spend my points on the launcher first, and don't upgrade to the final level of the belts/parts/etc until after that. Then, it's worth it to go back and redo the older milestones from scratch to really crank out the points, which eventually get to 10 per level earned. I finished the tree just after finishing the final milestone and letting it crank out about 6 levels.  
 
The downsides include a clunky UI with only limited keybinding control and slow, hard-to-memorize finger enchantments like {left-click-e-e-drag-q-q-release}x4. One cannot build one's own toolbars from the set of functions available. The blueprint save and edit system is also primitive and hard to use but does the job once one realizes one needs only a few real workhorse blueprints one can reuse over and over again. I admit I downloaded solutions from Discord and studied them to see how they worked before using them.  
 
I have completed the final certification milestone and completed all the research and a large percentage of the side tasks, but not all, nor am I likely to. I'm going to give the random milestone thing a try, but I am not interested in Make Anything Machines (my past profession) so a chunk of the content remains untouched by me. A recent dev blog about a possible new game mode and playloops shows the game has a lot to work with as is. I recommend it.

comment_evidence.clause: I decided to take advantage of the Steam sales and also purchase Shapez 1 which differs from its successor for 2D graphics and some small differences that do not preclude in any case commitment and fun in playing it
comment_evidence.full_review:
Da sempre sono un appassionato di puzzle game e due dei miei preferiti tra essi, sono Portal e Portal 2 che ritengo dei capolavori assoluti. 
Nei puzzle game, cerco solitamente un'adeguata curva di apprendimento ed un giusto livello di sfida ma al contempo, apprezzo poco i timer pressanti che scandiscono il tempo a disposizione, distogliendomi dal gia' oneroso sforzo mentale necessario al completamento del livello o della sessione di gioco del momento. 
Recentemente, ho visto in azione Shapez 2 girare sul Pc di un amico e me ne sono innamorato. 
Per chi non ha avuto modo di vederlo nei video online, Shapez 2 e' un puzzle game che permette grazie all'uso degli utensili a disposizione, di manipolare delle forme, all'inizio solamente di colore grigio, con lo scopo ultimo di completare le richieste principali e secondarie del gioco. 
Le forme che si comporranno, dovranno essere poi inviate, grazie a dei nastri trasportatori, all'interno del vortice presente al centro dell'area di gioco. 
Il gioco guida il nuovo player spiegando di volta in volta, come utilizzare gli utensili che aumenteranno di numero gradualmente, sbloccandoli con i punti che verranno guadagnati completando le missioni secondarie. 
Completando le missioni primarie, otterremo le ricompense principali e l'avanzamento di livello che offrira' nuovi elementi da utilizzare in gioco. 
Shapez 2, e' un gioco che mette alla prova l'ingegno e le capacita' del proprio cervello in modo fantastico, richiedendo calcolo ed ottimizzazione con lo scopo ultimo di produrre il piu' velocemente possibile le forme richieste e completare cosi' gli obiettivi richiesti. 
Il tutto, avviene senza fretta e per quanto non sia un idle game, non si sente la pressione di una tempistica limitata entro la quale soddisfare le richieste e nel corso della nostra sessione di gioco, verremo accompagnati da tracce audio spettacolarmente rilassanti e piacevoli. 
Dopo aver acquistato Shapez 2 Supporter Edition, ho deciso di approfittare dei saldi di Steam ed acquistare anche Shapez 1 che si differenzia dal suo successore per una grafica 2D ed alcuni piccole differenze che non precludono in ogni caso impegno e divertimento nel giocarlo. 
In conclusione, per quanto mi riguarda, Shapez 2 e' un gioco che vale la pena acquistare e che da italiano, ritengo che pecchi solamente per la mancanza del supporto per la lingua italiana. 
La mia scarsa conoscenza della lingua inglese mi permette di goderne comunque, ma per chi non conosce affatto una lingua straniera, questo potrebbe essere un problema e potrebbe allontanare una fetta di ipotetici acquirenti. 
 
Conclusioni personali 
 
Giocabilita' : 9 ( Ottima curva d'apprendimento ma potrebbe risultare in ogni caso difficile per alcuni ) 
Longevita' : 9 ( Tanti livelli da sbloccare e differenti livelli di difficolta' tra cui scegliere ) 
Grafica : 9 ( Ben realizzata e curata per quanto semplice possa essere il concetto di gioco ) 
Musica ed Effetti : 10 ( Il comparto audio, e' inappuntabile ) 
 
--- 
 
I have always been a fan of puzzle games and two of my favorites among them, are Portal and Portal 2 which I consider absolute masterpieces. 
In puzzle games, I usually look for an adequate learning curve and a fair level of challenge but at the same time, I do not appreciate the pressing timers that mark the time available, distracting me from the already onerous mental effort necessary to complete the level or the game session of the moment. 
Recently, I saw Shapez 2 in action running on a friend's PC and I fell in love with it. 
For those who have not yet had the opportunity to see it, Shapez 2 is a puzzle game that allows you to manipulate shapes, initially only gray in color, with the ultimate goal of completing the main and secondary requests of the game, using the tools available. 
The shapes that will be composed, must then be sent, thanks to conveyor belts, inside the vortex present in the center of the game area. 
The game guides the new player explaining from time to time, how to use the tools that will gradually increase in number, unlocking them with the points that will be earned by completing the secondary missions. 
By completing the primary missions, we will instead obtain the main rewards and the level advancement that will offer new elements to use in the game. 
Shapez 2, is a game that tests the ingenuity and the capabilities of your brain in a fantastic way, requiring calculation, planning and optimization with the ultimate goal of producing the required shapes as quickly as possible and thus completing the required objectives. 
All this happens without haste and although it is not an idle game, you do not feel the pressure of a limited time within which to satisfy the requests and pleasantly, during our game session, we will be accompanied by spectacularly relaxing and pleasant audio tracks. 
After purchasing Shapez 2 Supporter Edition, I decided to take advantage of the Steam sales and also purchase Shapez 1 which differs from its successor for 2D graphics and some small differences that do not preclude in any case commitment and fun in playing it. 
In conclusion, as far as I'm concerned, Shapez 2 is a game that is worth buying and that as an Italian, I believe that it only sins for the lack of support for the Italian language. 
My poor knowledge of the English language allows me to enjoy it anyway, but for those who do not know a foreign language at all, this could be a problem with the almost obvious consequence of alienating a portion of hypothetical buyers. 
 
Personal Conclusions: 
 
Playability : 9 ( Great learning curve but could still be difficult for some ) 
Longevity : 9 ( Lots of levels to unlock and different difficulty levels to choose from ) 
Graphics : 9 ( Well made and cared for as simple as the concept of the game may be ) 
Music and Effects : 10 ( The audio section is impeccable )

comment_evidence.clause: The animation is ugly in the precise
comment_evidence.full_review:
You’re a little guy. The town is wrong. Everyone needs help in a way that makes things worse. Every joke lands because it knows when to stop. The animation is ugly in the precise, intentional way that only confidence allows.

There’s no mechanical bloat, no fake depth, no anxiety about “value.” You walk around. You press buttons. Comedy happens. The game trusts you, which is rare, and rewards that trust with impeccable timing.
In an era of endless updates and hollow ambition, this is a finite object that understands itself completely. It’s funny, it’s sharp, and it doesn’t overstay.

comment_evidence.full_review: Thank goodness I played this game! What a time at Barnsworth, what I would imagine the developers at coal studio would assume would be the tone of a quintisential British town. Before I get ahead of myself, and despite me not having ADHD, the thing that kept going through my head was the fact that people with ADHD would absolutely adore or hate this experience. From the wonder of discovery of the next piece of town lore showcased to the player like Roger Peelings, the grocer insecure about his head or the price shagger sisters (to think that they would name a shop price shaggers - it is so irreverantly funny to me and yet absurd). The audio work was excellent and reinvegrated the love and joy I have for audio engineering and sound production, every squelch, squeeze, smack, smash, and snort felt incredibly snappy and crisp to the ear. Definitely an absolute highlight! The animation takes the cake here though. Too long have I yearned for a 2D game that looks and feels like an animated series without feeling like a walking simulator. This expertly blends what the pacing of a 22 minuite episodic animated romp should feel like with the scope, budget and timing available to the developers and players. With roughly 9 animators on the credits list my hat goes off. Th characters are unique, personable and hilarious; the sound work is excellent; the animation is of a tier so clean and unmistakenly British it warms me heart. Nevertheless, the gameplay might be the only bit that felt slightly lack luster. With an extremely detailed map with jokes and inuendos sprinkled everywhere I often got lost on where I needed to be heading as there is quite a bit of back tracking in this game between locations, however that is all part of getting to know Barnsworth. If the devs felt like people didn't know where they were going we probably would have had a mini map. The trippy sections were absolutely mind bending too and reminded me oh too well of the Good time Garden. Additionally, the game's mechanics revolve around walking around, extremely light platforming sections, smaking people (one of the most fun parts of the game, as each character has unique responses to smacking at different sections of the game), and specific mini-games taloired aroudn each bite sized narrative. Regardless, this game is worth it in so many ways. The were too many parts of it that resonated with me, talkless of the setting, which I imagine is usually only ever seen in a local context (thus the decision to localize everywhere makes sense from a sales perspective but baffled me as I imagine that this aesthetic is rather niche, however, this may just be how it explodes). The medly at the end with all the characters in the game constantly needed the help of the player before he can get a chance to see the mayor reminds me of how I tend to overextend myself. Being reflected in this way with the player was slightly saddening as he is mute and in the end must complete favours for the mayor before we ever get the chance to hear our character even speak. The need for this character in this society despite how he feels about his shortcomings reminded me about of the role I play in the lives of those closest to me. Taking on each challenge with a smile, no matter the gravity of the situation... MAN

comment_evidence.clause: I will probably mess around with the endless mode a bit and hope that the developers add some more content in the future since it’s a pretty good game that has a cool setting and great aesthetics
comment_evidence.full_review:
[h1][b]MULLET MAD JACK[/b][/h1]
[i]Mullet Mad Jack[/i] is a fast paced boomer-shooter roguelite set in the year 2095.

[b]Story [/b]

The game is set in the year of 2095 in which robot billionaires have taken over the world and humans are highly addicted to dopamine. The player controls Jack who is a so-called moderator who was hired by Peace Corp. to rescue the Influencer Princess who is being held hostage in a massive skyscraper filled with killer robots. The princess is located 10 floors above you and you only have 10 seconds to reach the exit of each floor, sounds easy right?

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3303877776
[b]Personal Note[/b]

I played the demo of [i]Mulled Mad Jack[/i] earlier this year and it instantly hooked me despite not being a huge fan of boomer-shooters but the fast paced action and the setting itself just made me like the demo a lot when I played it.

The game itself was released not too long after I’ve played the demo and I purchased it fairly shortly after the release. The game feels good. It’s fast paced and the gameplay loop is straight forward: Your timer ticks down, killing robots gives time – dopamine goes brr; or something like that.

Quite honestly the story itself is okay but nothing special, right? It kind of has the whole Mario vibe. You finish the 10 floors; you defeat a boss and the princess is [strike]in another castle[/strike] on another floor. Despite this sounding a bit whack, the story has certainly its moments, especially the epilogue and the whole premise of the game itself is quite interesting.

The gameplay loop is satisfying. The bosses are quite simple but can be a challenge on higher difficulties. Clearing a floor gives you an opportunity to buy new guns or new passive effects and defeating a boss grants you some permanent upgrades – so pretty standard roguelite elements that mix well with the whole fast boomer-shooter gameplay.

The upgrades that you get after every floor feel fair and nice. If you have a good gun and some good upgrades you will probably do more than well – especially in the endless mode in which your timer gets reduced by 1 second every 10 floors which makes the game harder after you’ve reached floor 40 since you will only have 7 seconds to complete the level; that means that getting hit and not instantly killing a robot could be fatal.

The art-style, the graphics, the music and the overall vibe of the game are great. It’s essentially a retro anime with a beefy male protagonist that yells those 90s action movie slogans every so often.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3303285477
The length of the game isn’t too crazy either. It took me around 3 hours to finish the game which is alright since there is the previously mentioned endless mode in which you can unlock some more cosmetics and if you like to go for achievements there is a few of them that require you to play through the game on higher difficulties and such – so there is replay value for sure. I hope that there will me some more content update in the future though.

Speaking of different difficulties: There’s also a difficulty which removes the timer and changes the gameplay from a fast first-person-shooter to a boomer-shooter that let’s you play the game without needing to worry about the timer and such. I personally think it’s a nice idea but it’s certainly not meant to be played like this but it might be fun for some people that have beaten the game already and want to try something new. There’s also an achievement for completing the whole game in that mode.

[b]Rating[/b]
[list][b]Pros[/b]
[*] The story is okay but has its moments
[*] Great aesthetics  
[*] Great soundtrack that fits the vibe
[*] Nice voice acting
[*] Nice mix of boomer-shooter and roguelite
[*] Endless mode 
[*] Upgrades feel fair
[/list]
[list][b]Cons[/b]
[*] A bit short
[/list]
[b]Conclusion[/b] 

Is [i]Mullet Mad Jack[/i] worth your money? Yeah sure. It depends on what you want from a game.

If you go after the whole “1 Euro = 1 Hour” thing I’d say that it’s best to buy it on sale if you only plan on playing through it once without messing around with harder difficulties or with the endless mode.

For me personally, I bought it with the 20% off deal and I have to say that it’s worth it for me. I will probably mess around with the endless mode a bit and hope that the developers add some more content in the future since it’s a pretty good game that has a cool setting and great aesthetics.

There should be a demo available so you could just mess around with that before you decide on getting it or not.

[b]7.9 / 10[/b]

“[i]Why is it always 10 floors?[/i]” - Jack

If you found this review helpful, feel free to visit my [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38665896/]curator[/url] page.

comment_evidence.clause: the UI is clunky and overdesigned and will often lead to your untimely death by covering up the important parts of the game
comment_evidence.full_review:
Mullet Madjack is a weird game that I'm unable to recommend.

The map variety is non-existent and the game is barely legible, the UI is clunky and overdesigned and will often lead to your untimely death by covering up the important parts of the game, the game is not difficult at it's core, it's just not all that playable if played the way it's intended. The hitboxes aren't tight and the level design is samey but not samey enough to be learned by heart. It's a good looking game but that's about all it is. The weapon balance is all over the place and if you're aiming for higher difficulties you'll likely find yourself going back to the only viable weapon in game, the fully upgraded starter pistol which lets you finish levels in a normal amount of time (20-30 seconds) and kill enemies in a speedy manner.

The gameplay is horridly shallow and the more interesting gameplay altering upgrades ( such as the grappling hook or environment items) fall short because the game wasn't built to accomodate them. In short, if you've finished the DEMO which is available, you've seen most if not nearly all of what the game has to offer.

Compared to other fast paced shooters on the market which fill a similar niche such as Deadlink or Roboquest, Mullet Madjack leaves a lot to be desired, the developer insists that this game has nothing in common with either of those titles but I beg to differ, there's way too much overlap not to take it into consideration. 

If you're a fan of wild visuals and weird shooters, MMJ might be up your alley, certainly not mine. I decided to embark on a journey to finish the game on HARD and then INSANE but I simply got bored of it, dropped the game for a few months and came back to finish it alongside the rest of my backlog and decided to drop it again. 

MMJ feels like an early access title sold as a finished product with a healthy dose of identity crisis. I'm not sure where the overwhelmingly positive reviews are coming from because the game is simply undercooked. It falls short in comparison to actual modern boomer shooter such as DUSK, Forgive me Father, ULTRAKILL, Project Warlock, Fortune's Run and many more, I can only attribute the positive reviews to the game's visuals.

I urge you to download the DEMO and consider if the free portion of the game ( which is more or less everything this game has to offer) is fun enough to be played through 8 times over for the game's asking price.

comment_evidence.clause: The art style is charming and very cute with each enemy you come across having a little tidbit of funny information and the cards being really well-detailed (and some really great goofy ones like a card with GIgachad)
comment_evidence.full_review: I was scrolling through the Steam Store page not looking for anything in particular, but then I stumbled upon this game and took a look at it. It looked interesting, and luckily, there is a demo to try out, so then I tried it out... I have been playing this game for 4-5 hours consecutively from demo to buying the full game and damn is it a lot of fun!! The art style is charming and very cute with each enemy you come across having a little tidbit of funny information and the cards being really well-detailed (and some really great goofy ones like a card with GIgachad). The way you can mix and match to find a build and class that is right for you opens soooo many opportunities that I have yet to get tired of! Not only that, you can unlock new things as you go and as well as simply anything can happen with each run being different from the previous one. The dice mechanic is so damn cool! I have not really seen anything like it before and it really works those creativity muscles. This game incorporates elements of RPGs, TTRPGs, roguelikes, and strategy, which all come together to be a really enjoyable game :) I will say, the full game is different from the demo with the HUD being more tidy and different mechanics being unlocked, so just a heads up on that! All in all, this is a great game for if you enjoy playing casually and seeing where things go, and it is a ton of fun, really. I'm off to adventure and put more hours into the game and discover more things in this wonderful game!!

comment_evidence.clause: It certainly holds it's own in terms of quality all while feeling distinct thanks to it's drastically different art style and "gimmick" dice focus adding both randomness and customization
comment_evidence.full_review:
I'll start by saying this game is a strong recommendation from me.  Everyone knows steam hours can be way off by leaving a game on while AFK, but at least 45 of those hours are active playtime and I'm still enjoying it.  That is fantastic for a $15 game.

Everyone knows that Slay the Spire is the flagship game for the rogue-like deck-builder, and is normally head-and-shoulders above of it's competition.  Diceomancer bucks that rule.  It certainly holds it's own in terms of quality all while feeling distinct thanks to it's drastically different art style and "gimmick" dice focus adding both randomness and customization.

My only real critique is that there is virtually no online community for the game, such as a forum or wiki to allow people to ask questions or look stuff up.  I would highly encourage the devs or publisher to invest in trying to cultivate one!  I think that could really help make this game feel like a staple in the genre that it represents so well.

comment_evidence.clause: the soundtrack is fantastic for working your way through a gigantic puzzlebox of a house and the graphics are stylized in such a way that even though they aren't groundbreaking
comment_evidence.full_review:
So, I just reached room 46 and the game has ended and I have very mixed feelings right now. 
 
Let's start with the good to great: the soundtrack is fantastic for working your way through a gigantic puzzlebox of a house and the graphics are stylized in such a way that even though they aren't groundbreaking, they fit the mood and feel the developers were certainly trying to go for.  Speaking of mood, the best way to describe this game is "explore a mansion pensively while sipping something warm."  This game is comfort food on an extreme level; easy to pick up and put down, relaxing to play, easy to take bite sized steps toward the goal (while also being deceptively difficult to actually accomplish said goal).  I wholeheartedly enjoyed my entire time playing through it. 
 
But now that I'm done, there's a bit of emptiness to it - the ending was nowhere near as satisfying as the journey and despite there being several puzzles in the house left to solve, there's not a lot of drive now that the central goal has been accomplished.  I got it on sale and I'm kind of glad I did; I certainly enjoyed the game and could recommend it highly with minimal caveats to just about anyone - but I also don't see myself ever picking it back up again.  I loved the journey; I didn't necessarily care for the destination once I got there, but I was glad I took the trip.  About as succinct a review as I could give on this one.

comment_evidence.clause: -unique and charming aesthetic matched with the ambient soundtrack makes for a pretty relaxing experience when you're not ripping your hair out or completely lost
comment_evidence.full_review:
blue prince is a 'game' that exists. it is impossible to digest. you will inevitably get lost or frustrated and maybe even give up (ok i say maybe, it's almost certain you WILL give up at some point). it really does sometimes feel like this game isnt wholly designed with the player in mind. despite that, i'm really glad this game exists in all of its elaborate audacious glory. this is NOT a recommendation to play the game, just my review. 

some other things i want to say besides my ominous evaluation of blue prince is that:

-the raw gameplay loop of building a maze with resource management and gimmicks is really fun and a really novel twist on the roguelite formula. bonus points for having deeper mazebuilding strategies touched on in a series of discoverable books throughout. to be frank a lot of this games' problems originate from this said gameplay loop, but i like that they risked something new even if it would be inherently imperfect.

-the rewards from early-mid puzzles hidden throughout the game feel good to get! they make stuff better! really encourages you to focus on the bigger picture. later puzzles don't *tangibly* reward you as much but at that point blue prince has you stuck in its grasp or you're a lucky one. the way the puzzles and the gameplay loop are simultaneously delivered to the player feels really interesting in a way i can't quite describe. though i can describe how it feels for late-game puzzles, frustrating! oops! inherent flaw with the core gameplay concept! (it's ok, i forgive you blue prince) 

-lore can feel quite overwhelming initially but uhhh it's pretty good! can't say much!

-unique and charming aesthetic matched with the ambient soundtrack makes for a pretty relaxing experience when you're not ripping your hair out or completely lost

comment_evidence.full_review:
I can understand why some people don't like this game, it's indeed frustrating, you spend 1 hour only progress a little bit, or maybe nothing at all. It's not for everyone.
For me this game is revolutionary, as someone constantly try new puzzle/adventure titles and most of the time give up after a while because have seen something similar, but for this game I foresee myself spend another dozens of hours without feeling bored. I guess the difference with my experience is that the generic mood and tone of the environment is very soothing while being mysterious, it hits me so the exploration itself is very enjoyable which compensates the frustration.
It also knows how to tease you in every little detail, from the almost endless mini games everywhere, to the 5 seconds of anticipation while digging a treasure spot, not to say leaving all kinds of possibility to "tomorrow", you feel you're not playing the game but immersed and become part of the world.
Great concept, great design, great production, really glad I decided to try it.

comment_evidence.clause: I also recommend downloading mods that speed up the repetitive animations and to give infinite rerolls
comment_evidence.full_review:
If you're here for the puzzles - look elsewhere. While there are some basic puzzles--basic logic, basic maths--and one Cryptic Crossword-style puzzle, most of the "puzzles" you'll find in this game come down to reading a memo with the answer on it and then applying that answer. Then, whether or not you have access to the relevant memo comes down to RNG giving you the right room with the memo in it.  
 
That being said, when you accept that it's not a puzzle game, and is instead a mystery adventure about collecting lore snippets and putting them together, it becomes a lot more fun. I also recommend downloading mods that speed up the repetitive animations and to give infinite rerolls, especially towards the end of the game where the thread of things to explore is drying up, and progress depends on specific kinds of room configurations. 
 
I do think, though, that more could've been done to flesh out how enjoyable the rooms are to actually be in. A lot of them are really well-designed as enclosed spaces, and it was lame to realise how many of them had nothing to do except generate basic resource pickups in the same spots, and how many fun changes were hidden behind super rare Upgrade Disks. I also disliked how few interactions there were with Crafted and Inventory items. 
 
I also wish more was done with Curses, Experiments, Stars, and Dares beyond--again--just modifying resources. 
 
Overall, I think it's a great idea with great direction, and I really hope it inspires a new and evolving subgenre of roguelites.

There's some good puzzles here but the randomness messes with the flow, and the story is trying just a little too hard in ways that annoy me. The core of it is interesting enough to have me try a few more times, but weird feelings on this one.

comment_evidence.clause: The stages where there ARE more striking visual differences between the shapes (like the Blind Date stages or stages with major characters that use unique accessories) make this issue all the more apparent
comment_evidence.full_review:
Extremely cute game! A lot of fun if you like logic puzzles and not overly long. For how adorable and well-polished the presentation is though, it does lack in a few areas. 
 
Firstly, the absence of a "remove all" button is fairly surprising. If you want to wipe the board and start over, you'll have to manually tug each shape from their spot and dump them back on the sides. The desire to flip the table and begin again didn't come up often, but when it did, I definitely felt the lack of this button. 
 
Secondly, the cursor when you pick up a shape is a bit deceptive. When you grab a shape, you cutely dangle them from your fingertips as you move them around. This can naturally lead you to wanting to place them on a square by aligning their dangling feet over the box. However, the cursor's actual position is still the dead center of the hand. This can lead to awkward moments on boards where the placement squares are tightly packed together in which you keep dropping the shapes on the wrong tiles or accidentally swap a shape instead of putting them down next to one another. It's not too bad - it's certainly not overly precise, but I had plenty of moments where attempting to swap shapes quickly ended with me shuffling around shapes I had no intention of touching, which can get very confusing when your pieces are fairly nondescript shapes! 
 
Thirdly, and this is a very minor issue, but the pieces being nondescript shapes CAN make some of the more complicated stages a bit tricky for visual learners. The game does a VERY good job of visually representing certain conditions on shapes, a superb feat of visual clarity, but there are conditions without visual tells (like the shapes that dislike certain odors). And when all the shapes look fairly similar to one another, I often found myself shuffling shapes around and ending up in the exact same incorrect configurations. The stages where there ARE more striking visual differences between the shapes (like the Blind Date stages or stages with major characters that use unique accessories) make this issue all the more apparent. 
 
Again, love the visual design of this game, and this is indeed a minor quibble, but I can't say it didn't impact my gameplay at all. I also can't say that adding even more visual tells would be the answer as that sounds like it would just become a visual overload. It's just kind of an issue baked into this design, and I respect that. It's a cute visual design and was no doubt much easier to handle for a smaller development team. 
 
Also final minor design issue: on the Coworking stages, if you put a shape with a large "conditions" card in the bottom left chair, if the conditions card is long enough it can totally block the chair that shape is sitting in and make it VERY hard to pick them back up again and move them. Thought I was almost soft-locked for a bit there! 
 
Overall, wonderful game! Loved it and none of the above issues stopped me from having a tremendous time. Great job!

comment_evidence.clause: This game is overall fun and quite charming with the art style and characters particularly Nat who we see the evolution of throughout the game seeing new places as well as making new friends to hopefully make their mark as an actor
comment_evidence.full_review:
A cute and fun puzzle game about shape characters living their lives in which you are tasked at seating them based on their wishes for the perfect arrangement offering a cozy yet semi-challenging experience. 
 
This game is overall fun and quite charming with the art style and characters particularly Nat who we see the evolution of throughout the game seeing new places as well as making new friends to hopefully make their mark as an actor. The game starts out with the various locales you'll encounter such as a bus, diner, movie theater, and many more locations where it'll start to ramp up in difficulty through the amount of characters you must arrange properly as well as the amount of criteria for where they would like to be sat best. The game offers some challenges with some later levels making me scratch my head and forcing me to completely change my way of thinking, offering a fun amount of challenge without being too harsh in its requirements. For how the game is arranged I had a fun time arranging Nat and their friends with some of my favorite levels being the bonus ones where you're taken to new locales and scenarios with my favorites being the NY first dates and picnic levels. 
 
It's hard to think about any qualms I may have given the short length of the title being able to be finished in an afternoon, but I suppose I can say that the game as is understood with the formula can be a bit repetitive the more you play with locales being the same simply with more needing to be arranged which adds onto each level's playtime. While you do not need to perfectly arrange everything to move on, the novelty of having everything set perfectly is enticing enough to want to stretch your brain's logic to proceed best forward. 
 
For achievements, the game mostly grants them based on story progression with some miscellaneous ones through interacting with the environment culminating into the final one which is acquiring a perfect score on each level. With some trial and error and taking a step back, it shouldn't be too difficult with this being marketed as a cozy puzzle game that can be stretched in terms of gameplay based on what you want to achieve within it. 
 
Overall, I had a fun and cozy time playing through Is This Seat Taken? I haven't played too many puzzle games so this is a good introduction to the sort of logic that can be followed when it comes to exercising your brain's ability to abstractly think about the problem in front of you. I can appreciate being able to have fun with a game as well as utilizing my cognition to its best ability to solve the puzzle leading to a satisfying feeling of completion. Although short and a bit repetitive, I can highly recommend this game for puzzle game fans or simply those looking for a cozy game in arrangement.

comment_evidence.full_review:
When I started playing this game it was really fun since I love puzzles, but some environments got quite repetitive after the third city except for the special levels. I understand this is an indie game, but honestly from the content I expected unique levels each time when that is not really the case. 

I wanted to complete the full game before posting this review to get my true final opinion, since this is not the king of game I would replay and honestly by the end it got boring for me. This is the kind of game that can give you a couple of hours of fun and I don't regret buying it, because for a while I did have fun, but is not a game I would necessarily recommend. But the concept can be quite fun at the beginning and it's really nice how you can have multiple answers to a same level, but is just not a game for me.

comment_evidence.full_review:
I love this game and I'd love dlc or a sequel!

I did find the classroom levels to be annoying as the characters didn't have visual cue for who they could or couldn't sit by so it was annoying on those levels where almost everyone had someone they couldn't sit next to. Obviously that's not a visual cue that can be easily added so I'd just limit the mechanic more compared to having 6+ people have someone they can't sit by.

Some levels with only one or two specific solutions were a little tedious to do but that is just how I feel personally.

Those are my only critiques! Overall I really love this game, the varying mechanics, and the cute art style! :)
Took me 6 hours to complete the game and get the achievements (which are simple to get).

[h2] Really engaging and not too involved for an idle game [/h2]  
 
 
[b] Pros: [/b]  
- Cozy artstyle that doesn't clash with working on projects in the background 
- Fish designs are both accurate and funny for the made up models 
- Progression is slow but not grueling 
- There are a good amount of easter eggs that, while not essential to game play, are still fun to find 
 
[b] Cons: [/b] 
- Not enough customisation: Although there is a good amount of character model customisation a lot of it is immediately accessible as it is tied in content. This can take away from any accomplishment felt from using the in-game currency to unlock decorations. Equally, in my opinion, there should be a lot more customisation options for both the boat and sushi shop

comment_evidence.full_review:
[h1]Fore-cast[/h1]
I've been into idler desktop games as of late simply because they're cozy and nice to have on the side of doing other stuff. Most recently I've played another one within the same fishing genre called "Idle Waters" (henceforth IW) and I think both games have a lot of charm to them. Obviously this review is for FtD and I'll probably write a separate one' for IW too eventually, but I will be making comparisons between the two for being very similar in genre and theme, as well as just having sort of an anchor point to paint a better picture.

[h2]Comparing Two Games[/h2]
Off the bat, IW and FtD both share pixel-based art and whilst FtD's art-style seems a lot more simplistic, it more than makes up for it with it's added mechanics for a cozier environment. Regardless, visuals will always remain one of the most subjective factors and I think both are great in their own regard.

So delving more on what I think makes FtD more cozy, where IW tends to utilize more common mechanics of the idle genre such as layers and layers of rarity of fish through different colors a la 'Pokemon Shinies', FtD varies their fish through weight which for a fishing game feels more immersive and gratifying seeing your lightest and heaviest records. Fish are sold directly in IW to pay for upgrades and progression is further substantiated through quests and getting specific fish/loot. FtD adds a layer of charm by selling it through making sushi somewhat akin to Dave the Diver minus the manual control beside selecting the fish for your menu. Both games feature an aquarium(s) where fish can be displayed and benefited from. IW's aquariums are massive random loot generators to mostly sell whilst FtD just generates currency passively and fish can be fed to speed or keep things up. This is where I will stop comparing the two and focus more on FtD exclusively and why I personally think it makes for a more enjoyable experience.

[h2]Fishing For Compliments[/h2]
I tend to be very whimsical on writing reviews, only writing one when I really think a game is deserving of it and generally when I'm in the mood for it. So there's personal reason why I'm writing it for FtD despite having played other similar games earlier and more. It's charm, immersion and potential truly stands out for me within this genre of games; desktop idlers as I like to call them. I could rave on in elaborate detail on all the factors that make this game special, but for reading comprehension and character limit sake I'm going to [b]try[/b] to condense it to bullet points.

🐠 [b][u]Content & Progression[/u][/b]
     🐟 Upgrades such as fish and new areas spaced out making progression feel gradual and much more rewarding.
     🐟 Bestiary (or is it Fish-tiary?) as a gallery with weight records for completionists.
🐠 [b][u]Layers of Coziness (Lots of details, small and big that add charm and or immersion)[/u][/b]
     🐟 Having to pick up fish from the ship that will jump/wriggle if left alone.
     🐟 Fish sold through sushi bar with visitors that request specific fish for upgrades.
     🐟 References and nods to games and media for sushi bar guests.
     🐟 Aquarium for displaying and currency generation where fish can be fed.
     🐟 Hatchery for breeding fish.
     🐟 Different kinds of bait.
     🐟 Clickable events (small and big) that float and drift on your screen for extra loot.
     🐬 Decoration and customization for your ship, bar, aquarium and even characters.
     🐬 Charming variety of different sized fish that look unique and distinct from each other.
🐠 [b][u]Accessibility and UI (more and better than what other idlers seem to offer)[/u][/b]
     🐟 UI can be scaled through settings or simply and quickly scrolling the mouse wheel.
     🐟 The game can run both in the foreground or background.
     🐟 Clicks/keys outside of the game registers as clicks in-game to boost activity.
     🦈There's a "Boat Only Mode" where everything can be hidden aside for the boat and clickable events; which can both be scaled and moved to anywhere on the screen. This is actually a huge factor and plus as it makes the game so much less obstructive by covering minimal space on your desktop allowing you to do so much more on your PC. Or even add charm by placing the boat on your taskbar, windows or have it blend with your wallpaper or other applications. (Shark bullet point for how big I think this is and unique from your average desktop idler).

There's probably more to mention that I might be overlooking or haven't gotten to yet this early in the game, but to me it's already more than a full package to warrant me writing this early review. Literally the only 'con' I could think that could be de-bait-able for some people is that things aren't fully automated (or yet, that I know) cause you do have to keep up supplies of bait and fish for the bar as well as picking up the fish through clicks or swiping. Maybe it unlocks or gets added in the future, but as it stands I don't see too much pressure or necessity in it with how cozy everything is; as it makes way for a more relaxing kind of playstyle than say a cookie clicker game where constant progression is key.

[h2]Reeling-it-in[/h2]
Nevertheless, the game still has so much more potential depending on what the devs decide to do or add to it. They could still add more depth and variety through some of the features of other idlers like IW (e.g. fish rarity/shinies) or other bits and pieces of either content or cosmetic variety.

In any case, I wholeheartedly support it and bought the supporter pack as well for that very reason. And I'd recommend it to anyone as a nice and cozy minimal space covering idle fishing game that could even serve as a desktop companion.

[i][b]It's ofishial: a fin-tastic game, breaming with coziness that any pun can get hooked on~

comment_evidence.clause: [b] 美术调整 [/b]：优化丑鱼设计（如哥布林鲨鱼）
comment_evidence.full_review:
[h1] 《悠哉钓鱼》真的悠哉吗？ [/h1]
正修343小时，终于全成就，撒花~

[h2] 推荐指数★★★★（4/5星） [/h2]
理由：创新挂机机制+萌系美术精准击中摸鱼需求，适合目标人群，但后期数值问题需优化，原价可入，打折更值。
[h2] 游戏概况 [/h2]
《悠哉钓鱼》是一款主打“桌面摸鱼”的挂机休闲游戏，融合钓鱼、养殖、寿司店经营等玩法。通过全局键盘/鼠标操作加速钓鱼、老板模式一键隐藏等设计，精准适配上班族摸鱼场景。像素萌系画风搭配丰富彩蛋增强沉浸感，但后期数值失衡（如升级费用过高）、自动化不足（手动操作繁琐）影响体验。开发组响应迅速，持续优化更新，适合碎片时间挂机。

[h2] 基础统计数据 [/h2]

[h3] 推荐/不推荐比例 [/h3]
- 推荐：549条（95.64%），不推荐：25条（4.36%），推荐比例显著高于不推荐，玩家普遍认可其挂机休闲定位。

[h3] 时长统计 [/h3]
- 推荐玩家：最长1176.1小时，平均263.2小时，中位数228.2小时（超200小时玩家占比高，黏性强）；
- 不推荐玩家：最长951.4小时，平均190.29小时，中位数124.2小时（部分玩家因后期数值问题弃坑）。

[h3] 语种分布 [/h3]
- 中文：532条（92.7%），英文：28条（4.9%），日文：8条（1.4%），韩文：6条（1.0%）；
- 好评率：中文96.4% > 英文92.9% > 日文100% > 韩文83.3%（小语种样本少，趋势参考性弱）。

[h2] 推荐理由 [/h2]
- 全局操作加速钓鱼：工作、打字时自动提升效率，实现“被动肝游戏”，正反馈强；
- 桌面适配极佳：窗口可缩放至角落，Alt+Q一键隐藏，摸鱼隐蔽性拉满；
- 多系统联动：钓鱼→养殖→寿司店闭环，满足收集与经营双需求，玩法轻量化；
- 开发组响应快：频繁更新修复问题（如新增服务员、自动喂食），诚意足。

[h2] 推荐人群 [/h2]

[h3] 适合 [/h3]
- 上班族/学生党（需要摸鱼神器）；
- 挂机游戏爱好者（如[i]《Rusty's Retirement》[/i]玩家）；
- 收集癖（全图鉴、成就党）。

[h3] 不适合 [/h3]
- 追求强交互、深度策略的玩家；
- 反感重复劳动、数值坐牢体验的玩家。

[hr][/hr]
[h2] 游戏优点 [/h2]

[h3] 玩法创新性与独特性 [/h3]
[b] 全局操作加速钓鱼 [/b]：键盘 / 鼠标点击（无论是否在游戏内）均能加快上钩速度，工作时也能 “被动推进进度”，同类少见（提及 127 次）；
[b] 老板模式 + 桌面挂机设计 [/b]：窗口可缩放至角落，Alt+Q 一键隐藏，完美适配摸鱼场景，隐蔽性远超同类（提及 89 次）；
[b] 多系统联动闭环 [/b]：钓鱼→养殖繁殖→寿司店售卖的流程完整，类似 [i]《潜水员戴夫》[/i] 但更轻量化，满足多元需求（提及 76 次）。

[h3] 品质与沉浸感 [/h3]
[b] 像素萌系画风 [/b]：鱼类、角色造型可爱，联动皮肤（如米塔、背包乱斗角色）增加新鲜感（提及 112 次）；
[b] 丰富彩蛋设计 [/b]：[spoiler] 海面漂浮物（海龟、宝箱）、猫咪讨鱼等互动，点击可获奖励，惊喜感强 [/spoiler]（提及 98 次）。

[h3] 核心玩法 [/h3]
[b] 离线收益优化 [/b]：后期更新支持养殖、水族馆离线运作，减少强制在线需求（提及 63 次）；
[b] 成就系统丰富 [/b]：全图鉴、一亿金币等长线目标，满足收集癖玩家（提及 55 次）。

[h3] 基础体验 [/h3]
[b] 开发组响应迅速 [/b]：频繁更新修复数值问题、增加自动化功能（如自动喂食、服务员扩招），玩家反馈被重视（提及 41 次）。

[h2] 玩家不满意的问题 [/h2]
[h3] 数值设计问题（重复可玩性） [/h3]
[b] 升级费用爆炸 [/b]：鱼竿、鱼饵满级需百万金币，后期金币无消耗渠道，纯 “坐牢”（提及 109 次）；
[b] 食谱升级反直觉 [/b]：组合菜需大量低级鱼，逼玩家囤货，收益常低于单卖（提及 87 次）。
[h3] 自动化不足（基础体验） [/h3]
[b] 手动操作繁琐 [/b]：收鱼、补饵、喂猫需频繁点击，违背 “挂机” 初衷（提及 121 次）；
[b] 服务员效率低 [/b]：单服务员难处理多桌，顾客因空盘卡住，收益受限（提及 73 次）。
[h3] 内容量与重复感（核心玩法） [/h3]
[b] 后期内容空洞 [/b]：五图钓完后只剩挂金币，无新机制，易无聊（提及 68 次）；
[b] 鱼种设计割裂 [/b]：现实鱼与奇幻鱼（如飞机鱼、奶茶鱼）混杂，部分玩家觉敷衍（提及 45 次）。
[h3] 争议点 [/h3]
[b]“伪挂机” 体验 [/b]：需频繁关注（补饵、喂鱼），与 “悠哉” 定位矛盾，玩家评价两极（提及 52 次）。

[h2] 玩家希望增加的诉求点 [/h2]

[h3] 自动化功能 [/h3]
[b] 自动补饵与一键收鱼 [/b]：减少手动操作，适配挂机核心（提及 143 次）；
[b] 养殖场批量投喂 [/b]：支持按数量选择饲料，避免重复点击（提及 89 次）。

[h3] 数值优化 [/h3]
[b] 降低升级成本 [/b]：鱼竿、鱼饵升级费用合理化，减少 “坐牢” 感（提及 119 次）；
[b] 增加金币消耗渠道 [/b]：如新装饰、DLC 内容，避免后期金币无用（提及 76 次）。

[h3] 新内容扩展 [/h3]
[b] 新增地图与鱼种 [/b]：扩展收集内容，如史前生物（托斯特巨型鱿鱼等）（提及 92 次）；
[b] 更多联动皮肤 [/b]：增加角色、船只外观，提升新鲜感（提及 63 次）。

[h3] 细节优化 [/h3]
[b] 图鉴说明与筛选功能 [/b]：标注组合菜材料、鱼的重量用途，方便规划（提及 78 次）；
[b] 美术调整 [/b]：优化丑鱼设计（如哥布林鲨鱼），增加装饰预览（提及 55 次）。
[hr][/hr]

[h2] 玩家提及类似游戏 [/h2]

《Rusty's Retirement》：像素风桌面挂机农场，支持后台点击加速，主打“摸鱼式养老”，适合喜欢慢节奏养成的玩家。

《潜水员戴夫》：深海探险+寿司店经营，融合动作与模拟，被称为“硬核版《悠哉钓鱼》”，适合喜欢深度互动的玩家。

comment_evidence.full_review:
It's a cute game, but I would never recommend this anyone at full price - only on steep sale. I played through it within about 9 hours, but like others said - it feels like a demo. 

There were some pros:
- I'm obsessed with organization so I had a lot of fun with all the different sections and how I wanted to cutomize my categories. 
- The gameplay was pretty smooth and the graphics were pretty good. It didn't feel like the AI cookie-cutter slop that you see in a lot of simulators.
- They slowly introduced new mechanics to parcels at a relatively good pace - enough that it kept me engaged for playing straight through without being bored.   
- Instructions were pretty clear, it does have a good pop up that appears when something new happens to tell you, but could've been a bit more indepth. I re-started my game a couple times as I overstickered which didn't meet the mission progression (not knowing you could delete/remove stamps.)

The negatives for me:
- Once you unlock all the areas and clean up all the parcels, that's it - there's no real ability to even continue playing. I've hit the front desk bell and no one would show up because there was nothing left to do other than cat-folk occasionally dropping off mail.
- Cat names/chat/requests are extremely repetitive and it lacks variety in characters
- I found parcels would get "wet" just by me picking them up on the ship, I'm not sure if it was them phasing through the boat, but it was a bit annoying.

This game has a lot of potential that could really give it more depth and make it really worth playing:
- A "free play mode" it so it can be a relaxing continuous flow to just organize and take care of the shop.
- Having parcels take on different appearances when damaged would be cool (soggy when not stored in the frozen area, bent if crushed by something heavy, etc.)
- Customers coming to the window themselves, creates a more "realistic/time management" kind of vibe; maybe can unlock multiple windows to create a bit of a faster pace for those who want it. Or having them line up so we can see if we have more time to organize/sort or if we need to focus the window.
- It would be good if you could earn money in game to purchase tools like carts, staff, purchasing additional "repair box equipment" etc.
- I almost wish you could purchase your own shelving to customize each section. I liked having a specific set up (pallets for heavy items, cubbies for fragiles, shelving for oversized items, slanted shelves for letters/flat parcels to easily see names). I disliked some of the shelving that I was restricted to and wished I could have set it up myself (much like Supermarket Simulator).
- Maybe customers need ID or a reference code; could add culprits like thiefs trying to steal mail when you can decline someone with non-matching ID; or a way to charge customers a fee. 
- Customizable or more stickers - being able to label boxes 1 of 2/2 of 2, would have been nice or sticks that you can make a note on - especially in challenges where you have "paired" boxes where 1 has to be in one environment and the second in another - neither can be moved. 
- Cycle different boats (maybe in different colours or with flags to indicate region) that alternate coming in to the dock throughout the day.; or maybe being able to "request" a destination point.
- Creating events (e..g, postal strike one area means a larger increase of parcels for x zone; holiday - larger increase of big parcels)

comment_evidence.full_review:
While this game is cute to look at, and I didn't hate the main gameplay functions, I would never recommend someone buy this. The short story is that for $15, you're simply not getting your money's worth. The gameplay is way too repetitive after the first few days, and the instructions are super unclear. Spend your money elsewhere, or hope they put in some updates to this game to fix the problems.

The longer problem list is here:

1. Instructions unclear:
Each new thing you need to worry about comes up with a little window that has a couple words with what to do, then only some show you exactly what it wants. This, however, is far from enough. My friend and I played through this not understanding that the packages ALL need to be sent out. The way it frames it makes it seem like you're supposed to KEEP everything except the ones customers give you, because it only says, "Fill the boat as much as you want", and not, "The things here may have people asking for them, but you're supposed to mail everything anyway". I will explain further on why that was made even more confusing, as this game makes you guess a LOT.

This confusion led to us having far too many packages to reasonably deal with, and made the game slower and a real chore. Which almost feels like they left it vague intentionally, because the game would be waaaaayyyy faster with that knowledge, as there is no real plot. I don't want to believe the devs want people to fumble just to milk their game for more play time, but the lack of detail on that action alone is wild to me, as it's the main function of the game, and as other reviews have said, has caused a lot of people confusion and dissatisfaction with the product. The tutorial needs an overhaul desperately.

2. BUGS:
Packages floating? YOU floating? Packages stuck somewhere, somehow taking up the air/shelf space AND some other spot? Too bad, no respawning can help you, and the save only happens every time the captain leaves, so good luck reloading without losing progress. Things bug out pretty frequently, whether it be the tutorial windows popping up all the time and needing to be dismissed again for no real reason, or the customers having weird blanks in their speech. Packages can also just get stuck in your hand, or in the far back of the awful shelving where you will have to find the EXACT right spot to click or that package is dead to you. Also, the packages in storage can sometimes just have new stickers appear on them, as I had looked through every shelf several times and never saw cold/hot stickers, then would go back and suddenly something would need to be put in the hot room???? The code in this must be spaghetti or something because it felt like that post office was haunted by a mean ghost more than anything.

3. The Guessing Game:
I learned only via reading other reviews that the customers can sometimes give you the wrong information???? Which is insane, because with the added confusion of not knowing to send all the packages, it leaves people with too much to look through. And, one of the bugs I didn't mention before, was that I could find the EXACT package the customer was asking for, only for them to turn it away and leave me stuck with MORE packages. That as well as them giving FAR too vague of info caused this to feel more like a real post office job (in the miserable way) than a cozy game should. Except, if I went to the post office and was that vague with them, I would be laughed out of the building! For a cozy game, I think the customers should at LEAST always give a last name, that way you don't have to bring up 12 packages to all be rejected and need to be put back into the awful storage situation. This feeds into my next two points;

4. The Shelving Crisis:
The boxes in this game have a decent range of shapes and sizes (none of which are clear enough for the customer to say, "I hope it fits on my bike" and for me to know what that means) but a lot of them are a true pain to find a space for. I realize the shelves are made more for people that figure out EVERYTHING is meant to be sent out, but I know from other reviews you can still end up with quite the pile, and the shelves are optimized about as much as the US Government, which is to say not at all. Big boxes hardly ever fit where they needed to, and sometimes the shelf LOOKED like it could stack two of the same kind, but, unsatisfyingly, it did not. Once more, for a cozy-type game, I feel like something way more satisfying would make the experience a lot nicer.

5. "Punishment" and "Progression":
There isn't really any punishment for messing up in this game. Which would be kind of nice, except there aren't really rewards, either. You get things to hang on the walls from the old postman, unlock more places for different types of packages (Which doesn't help much, somehow lol), and... That's it. No cosmetics, no power ups, no nothin'. Even the "story progression" is just digging through those piles to find the old postman, which is guessable from the second the game starts.

It dings you for damaging packages, but it's only a couple points that literally don't end up mattering even a little bit. The only other "punishment" you get is when you have to turn a customer away, the bell will take longer and longer for you to be able to ring it again. This being the only real "punishment" you get is only annoying at best, as with the bugs and everything else, I was made to often decline folks. They will wait literally forever for you to find a package, too. Though, I suppose that's a good thing since you have so many to dig through sometimes. Knowing that you're supposed to send things out (even things people will ask for?), makes this even worse as the only punishment, because the game is forcing you to just take it sometimes. It's not a mark on skill or anything like that, just a small annoyance that feels more spiteful than anything.

6: Messy Stickers:
I understand that not all packages will have the clearest to read stickers, as that's more realistic. However, especially on smaller stuff, the stickers would stack and cover each other. I would sometimes see a HINT of a sticker under another and realized pretty fast that if someone was asking for something from one of the special rooms, and I couldn't find it, it would be faster to just turn them away. I had zero desire to go and pick off EVERY sticker on every package to see if that's what they wanted.

Sticking them on myself when receiving them, also didn't feel great. Have a letter that needs SIX whole stamps? Find a small one in the awful side menu that pops up (that you have to click on almost every time to pull the tabs out) and hope you can cram all six plus the heavy and destination stamp. Good luck! It made me never want to use the "for fun" stickers because it was just more clutter.

Overall, this game has some promise, but it feels far more like I paid $15 for just a demo. The idea was there, and not much else. We played it through to the end to see if things would pick up, and now I'm wishing I realized much sooner that there was no up, only time ticking away on when I could get a refund. This is not $15 worth of a game, but could be if the devs are still willing to work on it. If you like something mindless and slightly annoying, then this could be the game for you. Otherwise, if you're looking for cozy and satisfying, look elsewhere.

comment_evidence.full_review:
I am enjoying this game, but the one thing that frustrates me and makes the gameplay feel more tedious than relaxing is that I have absolutely no sense of my progression. Most of the achievements are related to fairly early unlocks. There's no in-game menu that tells me what else I might be working on unlocking. You seem to earn "experience" at the end of each shift that unlocks things, but there's no visual interface that tells me where it's all going.  How many boxes are in the mail pile? How many do I have left before the next change is triggered? How many different delivery ports are there?  
 
This, and secondarily I want there to be a menu option that has the tutorial explanations because it took me way too long to figure out that the moon symbol on the x-ray machine is for packages that have to stay in the dark, not for packages that need to be cleansed of bad juju. The x-ray symbol doesn't match the constraint sticker. It was likely mentioned in the tool tip when I unlocked this, but I had forgotten between plays or didn't encounter a brand new "must be kept in the dark" package for a while after unlocking that feature.  
 
I also think they devs could do more with the mystery behind the whole game. You find a lot of decorations that go back on the walls, including photographs and such. But why aren't there additional story finds that go along with them? Writing on the back of the pictures, "how did this get here?" questions about post office signs, etc. As things stand, I worry that I'm going to be disappointed when I finally empty the mail pile and find out what happened.

comment_evidence.clause: It'd be nice if they at least added a collectible list when you start a level and open the pause menu since sometimes you won't know how many cards or newspapers or schematics are in each level so a list would be nice
comment_evidence.full_review: This game overall in my opinion was amazing the straight forward story the large catalog of levels to explore. This game is worth your time and worth the 100% completion. I always loved classic doom you get thrown into a room kill every enemy till you come out on top. I never had a problem with the gameplay even on the hardest difficulty. But bias aside it's not for everyone if you enjoy vast dynamic gameplay beyond kill everything in sight you'll quickly get bored of the repetitive gameplay. Once you play a level or two you've seen the whole gameplay loop outside of the occasional new weapon, ability and gimmick. The baseball game is a shining factor of repetitive gameplay it's a nice novelty but if you want 100% be prepared to sit in front of that game for an hour more if you don't already have all the cards. This game is not serious in the slightest you play as a Private Investigator (It says so in the title lol). But don't expect to be piecing things together you collect clues and Jack does the rest of the work toward solving the mystery. In my opinion I don't mind that you don't do any real detective work outside of collection and side quest I prefer collecting the clues and getting to the next level set. A guide isn't really required it's possible to find all the collectibles naturally if your clever enough. Some of the secrets are very hidden. It'd be nice if they at least added a collectible list when you start a level and open the pause menu since sometimes you won't know how many cards or newspapers or schematics are in each level so a list would be nice. I can only pray for a future update. Beyond that my only real problem with the game is that I want more of it. The characters all have witty dialogue the references to old media and even the constant stream of cheese in this game is all very enjoyable it really gave off that old animation vibe even without mentioning the visuals cause the visuals speak for themselves they are amazing. I don't even need color in this game to appreciate the art. This studio is overall amazing and it shows in their work. Even after playing this game so many ideas sparked in my head for extra content. Rather it be a DLC or maybe even a co-op split screen mode maybe not for the main story but in a mini game aspect. Or hell even a battle mode where one plays as Jack and the other plays as the hitman in a pvp arena with weapons and cover. Or even just who can kill the most enemies in a limited amount of time in a small portion of a level from the main story like western backlot. I can definitely see a VR port made by the community for this game I can picture it exactly like the VR mod in GZ Doom. 3D environment with the flat 2d guns the music would really immerse you as if you really were Jack pepper. There are tons of other things I haven't mentioned but there's just so much to talk about don't knock the game till you try it you might be surprised what a simple shooter like this can offer.

comment_evidence.clause: - Absolutely beautiful art - All the "Interactable" assets in this game are 2D sprites and they always rotate to the player direction exactly as it was in Doom and Wolfenstein 3D where dead bodies were always turning towards player's camera
comment_evidence.full_review:
[h1] Non-IGNorant Review 16/10 [/h1] 
 
A love letter to the generation who grew up with hand drawn cartoons before computer animations mixed with the only shooter game we had called Wolfenstein 3D until later Doom arrived. 
 
[h3] The Good: [/h3] 
- Absolutely beautiful art - All the "Interactable" assets in this game are 2D sprites and they always rotate to the player direction exactly as it was in Doom and Wolfenstein 3D where dead bodies were always turning towards player's camera. 
 
- Around 10-20 hours of gameplay if you play on Hard. 
 
- Guns do not share ammo which is amazing, you can always switch to other guns if you run out of ammo from one, although the Pistol and SMG have the same bullet model but they do not share ammo which is really good for boss fights. 
 
- A lot of exploration. 
 
- No health regeneration, pure classic health pickup! 
 
- Too many various boss fights! 
 
[h3] The Bad: [/h3] 
- This is my personal opinion and not a negative point but the mission in Hell is very unrelated to both story and the game but it is just there to give you some Doom feeling. 
 
- The last 3 guns which are really advanced unlock way too late in the game that you almost never get the chance to use them. 
 
[h3] The Ugly: [/h3] 
- There is no sequel as of now!

comment_evidence.clause: One of the main reasons why I play a game has to be the art style and this stood out to me when I had seen a long time supporter talk about it (That NPC that appears in one of the levels telling you where the main bad guy went
comment_evidence.full_review:
This is genuinely one of the games of all time , joking it has to be one of my favourite games of all time and that's sitting beside Outer Wilds. I usually don't play shooters since I'm not too good at it but the movement along with the variations of weapons , made me want to swap between the few and i might ramble so let highlight some stuff i love!  
A. I LOVE the art style so much  
One of the main reasons why I play a game has to be the art style and this stood out to me when I had seen a long time supporter talk about it (That NPC that appears in one of the levels telling you where the main bad guy went , they made a NPC after her which is so so cute and thoughtful!) The weapons and set designs of the world is so stylistic I sometimes spend half the time walking around and looking at the surroundings more than playing LOL !  
 
B. Worldbuilding and the story 
I'm a massive achievement getter so I strived to get every single comic and newspaper collectible to the best of my ability ( I might have to replay to get the mouse funko pops i only found like 2 lol) I enjoyed reading the little snippets of newspaper articles and learning about the world through dialogue and the surroundings ! Some parts of the game may be whacky and honestly I didn't expect some portions but it was enjoyable and the whackiness really added to the charm of the game!  
I love the detective genre so the whole mystery aspect of the game kept me really engaged and I end up making my own little theories about what happened and the whole story unravelling had me so invested I tell my parents about it and think about it from time to time when I'm on my job.  
 
C. The Level design!  
I am truly impressed by the expansiveness of the levels and the amount of secrets you can find in each one! I took my time to comb through every level given and the variations of places really had me so engaged ... honestly with no spoilers - it covered places that you wouldn't expect! ( I really want to say but please play the game it's so fun)  
 
D. Pacing  
The pacing of the game was something I appreciated as the levels can be wrapped up in an hour or so ( an hour for me because i keep backtracking making sure I don't miss stuff out) , I played this game during work days so it was convenient for me to pick up where I had left off and I didn't have to worry much about forgetting where I had stopped.  
 
Now the good things are over here are some parts I had a little difficulty with:  
A. Not too clear as to where to go  
Honestly this might be on my part because I forgot I was given that brush thingy and sometimes it's not too clear what exactly I am to do during boss fights .  
However I do figure it out after a bit but I wish it was more obvious ( or i might be too concentrated i missed out stuff ( most probably, not gonna lie ) )  
 
B. Minor bugs  
I had a sprite of a baseball bat goon chasing after me for quite abit in which I couldn't kill it and it kept hurting me LOL  
it disappeared as soon as I accessed the next area so that's that.  
There were also timing issues with the subtitles and cut scenes , where the subtitles and cutscenes moved WAAAY faster than the audio  
 
These are minor stuff but I thought I'd add it in for a fair review! (Some in which might be a me problem lol)  
 
 
If you skipped everything to read my last part of the review here's a condensed version:  
 
I enjoyed the art style, worldbuilding, story, level design and pacing of MOUSE P.I For Hire a lot! I felt that it was masterfully crafted and such a joy to play through, yes while there could be areas to improve on, this game was very worth my 16 hours ( as of writing) and $20 (which i bought during a sale) .  
 
Thank you to the team for making this game, I am happy to be able to play a game that has so much love and thought put into it ! Truly enjoyed it a lot and am looking forward to future projects ! <3

I like the concept and the execution of the old style black and white for this fps, i love the themes and i am a sucker for P.I. detective stories.  
I liked the little map for stage selection.  
i did find a couple of bugs that worked in my favor so to say and this may be due to own eyesight but at some points the blending of the background items and all the environment made it hard to me to perceive depth, maybe it is patched into giving some shading to some background elements, i also turned the grain in the graphic setting to the max and helped me a little. 
Second comment i would thing might had need some work, most of the characters have very same generic face. i would had like for some of them have more unique designs specially for Jack. 
*Spoiler comment*. i loved the wizard of oz transition. it took me a minute the first time. and it made me wish more parts of the game had this kind of transitions but i get it. it is the game aesthetic and it is why i got it in the first place. 
 
Highly recommended. nice work.

comment_evidence.clause: the graphics are absolutely stunning and it was so much fun exploring each area for the first time and just being awestruck with the amount of creativity and love that has been poured into every inch of this world
comment_evidence.full_review:
Finally finished 100%ing this and wanted to give my thoughts. Overall I had a hugely positive experience, I love this series and have played both games in full, but there's a few quality of life changes and issues that are seriously holding this back.

The positives: 
God this game is so charming, the graphics are absolutely stunning and it was so much fun exploring each area for the first time and just being awestruck with the amount of creativity and love that has been poured into every inch of this world. 
The weather is a nice new addition and we can finally collect resources without building a machine and waiting 15 real life minutes for it to spit something out!! Oh my god thank you! 
Bea is fun to control (minus a few minor grievances which I'll touch on shortly)
And the game actually has an ending this time! It has its issues (again I'll touch on this) but with the last game just abruptly putting a credit scene in your face after opening more mail I don't care about it is so nice to have an actual end climax which utilises the tools and mechanics that we have been using all this time!

Now the negatives: 
The tarr are seriously annoying and need to be fixed, this was an issue in the last game too but it is even worse here. I like the idea of an enemy in the open world- and that it also serves as a punishment for mismanaging your farm is really good game design. The issue is how it's executed, "tarr slimes" form when a slime eats more than 1 different type of plort (the gem they spit out when they eat), in open ares food, slimes and ports are EVERYWHERE and its so bad that you genuinely cannot spend more than 30 seconds in one area without a tarr outbreak, it has ruined resource collecting, finding rare slimes and just irritates me every time I here their music start because they aren't a real threat they're just a nuisance that I'm constantly having to take time to deal with. An easy fix would be to just lower the rates at which slimes not on the farm eat plorts, and in return make the tarr much more dangerous to level out them being more uncommon.  

The tarr have never so much of dented my healthbar, but you know what has killed me multiple times? The annoying delay before your stamina refreshes and you can fly again. Like I said Bea controls well, but the stamina refresh is ridiculous, this game expects you to do a lot of jet pack flying so what this means is you fly for a couple of seconds and then have to sit and wait for god knows how long before you can move again. I know theres an extremely late game upgrade for this, but that isn't a fix in the slightest because you've probably finished the game before you can get the resources for it. Dying unfairly is never not annoying.

And finally the ending area, I'll try and keep it as spoiler free as I can but this was just frustrating, I enjoy the final area of this game more than I did in the last one, again its beautifully designed and I was required to spend a lot more time in this area than I was with the final area of the last game. But good lord is it a slog, the only way you find out how to progress is through LOTS of written text which is hidden throughout the world, which I'm really not a fan of in games. Text should be to the point and easy to access, but more importantly games should be using visual clues and show don't tell to guide the player. I ended up having to look up tutorials for the last couple of puzzles because I genuinely could not fathom out what the game wanted to me do to OR how on earth to navigate the extremely large and busy area.

Overall despite this review being quite negative heavy I do recommend this game. I love this series so much which is why it's so irritating that there are such big issues, if there's ever a third instalment I will 100% be getting it, Slime Rancher 2 improved the first game so much and it makes me feel very positively for any upcoming instalments or DLC in the future, I just really hope they iron out some of these issues.
