comment_evidence.full_review:
This game is very fun, relaxing and highly addictive but isn't without my small little nitpicks which I'll get into later in the review.

First the graphics in this game while simple they are very stylized making them very visually appealing while still giving a lot of character and life to the tanks you create and the fish you will hatch, breed and sell.
The animations of the fish and tank decorations really gel well together and you can easily create some beautiful tankscapes.

The Gameplay loop is very simple but highly addictive as even when you obtain a fish for your fishdex the game encourages you to constantly keep breeding fish for rare variants of fish known as "unique" which is this games version of shinies from Pokemon.
Every fish also has 3 stats each one individual to the fish you catch/hatch ranging from 0-100 those been:

Size - the bigger the fishes size stat the more it sells for
Fortune - Higher stat equals more money produced per hour
Fertility - higher chance of breeding 2 fish and shorter cooldowns for breeding

These stats while not at all important you can play this game while completely ignoring them if you wanted to add another layer of addiction that keeps you coming back as every fish you breed with another will pass down it's stats to the offspring meaning you can selectively breed fish with other fish to pass down good stats and work your way up to getting a perfect 100/100/100 stat fish which again you can breed and produce many more perfect 100/100/100 fish which yes you can get a perfect stat unique and that has been my addiction trying to get 1 of every unique perfect stat fish.

All of that been said there is no right or wrong way to play this game which I like.
Whether you just want to build beautiful fish tanks with all your favorite fish, min max every fish to perfection through breeding, hunt down every variation of fish to complete your dex or just chat with friends and do some simple fishing it's all a valid way to play and enjoy the game and you won't feel like your falling behind be it you don't engage with the deeper stats and mechanics of the game and just play how you want.

If you are someone who is a aquarium hobbyist like me you will know that irl fish keeping has a very strong social community be it online or irl.
Many hobbyist are always sharing tips, advice, trading fish, shrimp, snails, plants, equipment etc with each other.
It's not uncommon if you have a good brood of Neocaridina shrimp or maybe your guppies have been going at it like rabbits or you just have more java moss than you know what to do with to give new and established hobbyist some of your spoils this is one thing I have always loved about keeping tanks and I feel like this game really encapsulates that sense of community perfectly in the digital form.

Needless to say for the full asking price of this game it's a steal you will not regret picking it up especially if anything I've said sounds appealing to you in anyway.

Now for my nitpicks.
First the elephant in the room which many people I've seen in the discussions bring up there is not enough storage or tanks.
As of writing this I am level 26 so only have 5 tanks but in total there is only 11 in game.
Despite all my tanks been fully leveled up and having max storage to my current level I find myself having to get rid of fish I really don't want to get rid of due to a lack of tanks and space.
As someone who is very much into breeding perfect fish and trying to get 2 of every unique with perfect stats and keeping them all organized in their own tank (numbers 1-15 in the unique dex then 16-31 etc) this restriction is extremely frustrating.
As of right now my tanks are all disorganized due to a lack of tanks I'm having to constantly hot swap fish in and out for storage for breeding and as of right now I have no space to keep my fish I want to sell on the market place.

PLEASE DEVS GIVE US MORE TANKS AND AT EARLIER LEVELS I BEG YOU!

The other nitpick I have is the online market place, while great in theory I feel like it needs work.
In order to buy fish from other players you need a separate currency shells you can earn shells via leaving reactions on other players tanks, up to 5 reactions per day and selling fish to other players via the online market.
The issue is trying to sell anything on the market feels impossible.
First reason is you need to have the fish you want to sell in a tank which as I was saying is hard when you are already limited for space as is.
Then trying to find a buyer is also hard because the only good way of earning shells is through selling fish and therefore established dedicated players with abundances of perfect stat fish and uniques who just idle in fishing lobbies 24/7 (and I mean yes they literally just AFK for days at a time) are the only ones people buy from.
It feels impossible to be seen by other players due to established players having more tanks therefore more fish available to buy, more experience therefore tanks full of perfects and uniques and if you aren't actively using discussions and spamming the chat (which is very annoying btw don't do that) you're basically invisible everyone will just go to the established AFK traders who leave the game running for days on end.
This creates a cycle of:
>Try sell my fish to another player for shells
>Nobody buys my fish
>I don't have many shells and therefore don't want to spend what little shells I do have

It doesn't help as well that there's cosmetics you can only buy with shells further encouraging you to horde your shells and not spend shells on other players fish as you're saving your little daily amount you get up for the cosmetics.
The whole market place needs a rework in how players get seen in the market place and how shells are rewarded to actually encourage more trading among players imo.
Maybe like receiving reactions rewards shells and not coins and having a searchable market place that allows players to see listed fish for sale by other players.

The only other nitpick I have is why when fishing can't I have my caught fish directly sent to my storage so I can view them later to decide if I want to keep them or not?
Every time I go fishing I have to put an entire tank of fish into storage just so I can differentiate between the fish I just caught and ones I had in my tank.
It's very frustrating.
As well why can't we just see the stats of the caught fish before we sell it/put it into our tank?
Again just a really annoying little thing.

It would be lovely if we could fish and have the option to put the fish straight into storage and then be able to open up the storage menu without leaving the lobby to see the stats of each fish and decide from there if to sell it or not.

Apart from those few things, I really do truly love this game and I recommend it to anyone who is even vaguely interested in the aquarium keeping world.

Encase anyone wants to visit my aquarium here is my ID: 76561198293616927

comment_evidence.full_review:
This is a cute relaxing little idle game that just about anyone can get into- and I should know, I shared this with my mother and eventually had to buy her a copy just so I could get back to my aquarium.

The overall game loop is very simplistic. You have an aquarium (eventually a few aquariums) that you put fish in. You get fish by either buying eggs, breeding any two fish together, or going out into either the ocean or the swamp to fish. Any fish in your aquarium will passively generate gold over time that you can then use to get upgrades or more fish eggs. You have an infinite supply of food to feed your fish and a sponge to cleanup any algae spots that appear on the tank. Slowly through feeding your fish or finding new fish you'll level up, which opens up more upgrades and tank design options.

Overall, it's a really cute game that I've often left running in the background. In the settings there's a quick button to turn off UI giving a screensaver effect or shrinking the game down so you can have your aquarium sitting on your desktop.

comment_evidence.clause: gives you some very basic instructions on how to use the interface and otherwise relies on the player's intuition and actually works like you'd expect as opposed to having a long and detailed tutorial
comment_evidence.full_review:
I'm not very far into the game yet, but it starts nicely, gives you some very basic instructions on how to use the interface and otherwise relies on the player's intuition and actually works like you'd expect as opposed to having a long and detailed tutorial. The puzzles are categorized by difficulty, the harder ones being more interesting and needing more time to solve, whereas the easier ones can be solved in seconds, but there's still always some kind of novelty or insight to them so even the easier puzzles are entertaining to speedrun through.

So far, it looks like the video on the store page is a bit misleading with how much it focuses on the 3D graphics especially at first. I haven't spent very much time in that 3D environment at all, it's mainly just a really fancy level selection screen and most of my time has been spent looking at the 2D puzzles instead. As far as gameplay is concerned, this is absolutely fine, because if you're playing a puzzle game by Lunarch for any other reason besides the puzzles, you're probably doing it wrong.

comment_evidence.clause: This overworld might not have the most expensive graphics but it is beautiful to look at with lots of details and together with the gentle music creates a very nice and relaxing atmosphere
comment_evidence.full_review:
For people who played the previous game of the developers, Islands fo Insight: 
If you loved the logic grids in IOI, you will love this game. That is probably all you need to know.

For people who haven´t played Islands of Insight: 
The Artisan of Glimmith is a grid-based puzzle game. Your task is always to divide the grid into different regions (either by drawing borders or using colors) while satisfying certain rules. The end result is a colored grid that (thanks to the stained glass theme of the game) is often very pleasing to look at. There is a great variety of rules for the puzzles, ranging from size or shape constraints for your regions to rules about neighboring shapes and different symbols on the grid that introduce additional regularities. All these rules make for a great diversification of puzzles, especially when these rules are combined. The range of difficulties goes from very easy where you solve puzzles in under a minute and enter a flow of solving puzzles up to very hard  challenging puzzles that require all your knowledge about the implications and tricks of the different rule sets. The developers always stress that every puzzle is handcrafted and you can really sense that in the puzzles what makes this game so impressive and the puzzles feel fresh. Whether a puzzle is designed to teach you a certain trick, undermines your first intuition how the solution will look like or requires a certain insight to be solved, you often feel that intention of the designer of the puzzle.

The puzzles itself are scattered in an isometric overworld that you have to explore to find all the puzzles. This overworld might not have the most expensive graphics but it is beautiful to look at with lots of details and together with the gentle music creates a very nice and relaxing atmosphere. This also creates a nice change of pace so that you are not getting burned out from looking at puzzle grids all the time (A problem that at least I often have with very minimalistic and abstract puzzle games). 

The game offers quite a lot a freedom when it comes to choosing the puzzles. Usually in each area you are required to solve a few simple "tutorial puzzles" that teach you the new rules and are very quick to solve. After that you can choose from a wider selection of puzzles. When your total count of solved puzzles in that area exceeds a certain small number, a new area with new rules is unlocked and you can proceed to that area or choose to tackle some of the optional higher difficulty-level puzzles. I quite like this systems that lets you go back and forth between the different areas and makes sure that you almost always have a broad selection of puzzles to choose from with different difficulties and rule sets.

comment_evidence.clause: It's a bit disappointing that you can't actually walk around and explore the environments
comment_evidence.full_review:
Just download the demo and if you're anything like me, you'll only play it for a few minutes and then immediately jump out to buy the full game.

It's a bit disappointing that you can't actually walk around and explore the environments, because the trailer makes it look like you can. That being said, the game still looks amazing and comes with a stunningly beatiful piano soundtrack. There are hundreds of puzzles in the base game, with excellent designs and creative rule variants that are gradually introduced to keep things fresh, and workshop support could add infinite replayability.

Highly recommended to fans of logic puzzles like Slither Link or Nurikabe.

comment_evidence.clause: It's one of the most impressive RPGs I've played with beautiful pixel art environments and animations and I was hooked from beginning to end to get all achievements
comment_evidence.full_review:
Really terrific RPG full of attention to details both large and small scale and full of content. Rewards thinking ahead or outside the box frequently with many choices to navigate problems. It's one of the most impressive RPGs I've played with beautiful pixel art environments and animations and I was hooked from beginning to end to get all achievements.

Do just note if you're interested in this, this isn't a full-scale prison sandbox. While there is room for choices and branching paths of escape, it's primarily a story-focused RPG where the prison serves as puzzle obstacles to navigate through skill check rolls and planning. The game has a 21 day time limit due to each day having unique events, inmate dialogue and small prison modifiers, but the time limit is reasonable and the game has a New Game + like Dead Rising to take skills and experience to a new run if you fail. If you think you might be interested I can't recommend this enough.

comment_evidence.clause: The sprite work is great and the animations are really fluid so a lot of work went into that above a lot of other sprite based games
comment_evidence.full_review:
Fun time management game.  I played though Thomas' route and may get to Bob's one day.  The sprite work is great and the animations are really fluid so a lot of work went into that above a lot of other sprite based games.  Music fits the game but there was nothing for me that was outstanding.  And the story was fine enough, the inmates are generally distinct enough that it's neat to learn about.  There's a lot of elements influenced by shows and movies like Prison Break and The Shawshank Redemption.

The actual game play is sub divided into main story objectives and then securing an escape route.  There's a lot of different routes that you can take and find.  But the game does somewhat feel like you need to go through and fail once and try again because there's a lot of initial discovery to figure out where things are, what leads to what, etc.  And the 21 days is very tight in a NG run when you don't know exactly what you're doing.  It's doable but I think you have to play somewhat aggressive and work on getting bonding with the other inmates to learn a few critical skills.

NG+ makes it a lot easier because learned skills and existing bond carries over which can be a big boon with the right ones as not all skills are created equally.

My only real complaint is that the save system only saves a single prison day so while I'm interested in exploring other ways to escape even on NG+ it was starting to feel sloggy since it takes ~15-20 hours from start to finish.  If I could just roll back enough to skip the first handful of days when things really start to diverge it would have been great or some sort of speed up feature so just running around you just booked it faster.

But if you enjoy time management games and have an interest in daring escapes then could be a good pick up for you.

comment_evidence.full_review:
Back to the Dawn" - A Hidden gem among prison roguelites

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Web review with screenshots below. If this review helps you, feel free to follow my Steam Curator for more reviews.

WEB REVIEW - https://solo-save.com/2026/02/22/back-to-the-dawn-a-hidden-gem-among-prison-roguelites/
CURATOR - https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44944862/

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Back to the Dawn is a hidden gem that caught me off guard with its intriguing concept and atmospheric prison setting. The game offers a compelling narrative that keeps you engaged from start to finish, exploring different combinations of skills and different outcomes.

The pixel art graphics are a standout feature, adding a nostalgic charm to the game and effectively conveying the dark and oppressive atmosphere of the prison setting. The pixelated visuals are well-executed and add to the overall immersion of the game.

The concept of "Back to the Dawn" is undoubtedly its strongest suit. The idea of navigating through a prison and unraveling the mysteries of the protagonist's past is both compelling and original. The game successfully creates a sense of isolation and desperation, making you feel the weight of the protagonist's circumstances.

However, there are a few areas where "Back to the Dawn" could have been improved. The randomization of certain elements in the game feels a bit disjointed and could have been implemented more seamlessly to enhance the gameplay experience. Additionally, while the pixel graphics are well-done, the medium-level visuals in between can sometimes feel lackluster, and the overall graphics quality could have been better optimized.

One of the major drawbacks of the game is its limited replayability. Once you've completed the main storyline, there's little incentive to revisit the game due to the lack of alternative paths or endings. This is a missed opportunity, as a more dynamic narrative structure could have added significant replay value to the game.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

🏆Overall: ( 7 / 10 )

Back to the Dawn is a hidden gem that offers a unique and engaging narrative experience despite its flaws. The atmospheric prison setting, compelling storyline, and charming pixel graphics make it a game worth exploring. While the replayability and graphics quality could have been better, the overall concept and execution are strong enough to make it a memorable gaming experience. Don't let this underrated title slip under your radar.

comment_evidence.full_review:
TLDR; 10/10 if you like RPGs, Point and Click adventures, and well told stories featuring anthropomorphic animals.  
 
As a disclaimer, I received a review key for the game, and thus did get the game for free, but am by no mean required to give this a positive review. But after 50+ hours and going into my second playthrough, I must say the blend of RPG, point and click adventure, and mild resource management in Back to the Dawn has definitely surprised me. I wasn't expecting much when coming into the game but was looking for something different, and Back to the Dawn did just that. 
 
Whats not to love about this game 
 
Multiple paths to end game that add to replayability 
The visuals are a fun retro pixel art style that gives that nostalgic feeling 
Each NPC has their own wants a needs to discover across multiple playthroughs and a 
NG+ that carries over relationship progress with NPC's to unlock new skills 
and the soundtrack is catchy and fun, yet not so much so to be distracting. 
 
There's a lot to discover here even in it's early access state. The menu is pointing towards other characters being playable in coming updates and I'm very much looking forward to exploring even deeper into the lives of the inmates and seeing how some of the other stories play out. After multiple Twitch streams I had multiple community members buy the game and have all been thoroughly enjoying their time with Back to the Dawn

comment_evidence.clause: I want to recommend the game because it has great mechanics and graphics
comment_evidence.full_review:
I want to recommend the game because it has great mechanics and graphics. 

However, I have yet to have a single run that doesn't easily +10x the targets just pressing auto play + end turn. I can afford to empty out the store slightly past the midgame. There is a HP mechanic but I almost try to spend as much HP as possible because healing is abundant. Doesn't matter the difficulty, doesn't matter the build, doesn't matter if I pivot mid game.

There are simply to many opportunities to easily build around every mechanic, cards can be sold at will, and there are no particular difficult boss mechanics.

The game is simply too easy - by a huge margin. Even endless mode is trivial.

comment_evidence.clause: This leads to weird situations like being able to draw from a deck before certain cards are added or being able to move items around in the middle of the animations being played
comment_evidence.full_review:
The game is a lot of fun if you are into games like Slay the Spire or Wildfrost. As you progress you expand your grid and on each tile you are able to place an item, animal or plant which have different abilities and synergies. It took a moment to fully grasp how the game worked but once you understand it, there are so many viable options.

My only criticism so far is that the game seems poorly optimised so hopefully there will be some performance updates soon. My PC runs a 5080, 32GB of RAM and a Ryzen 9 9950X3D, so it is absolutely no slouch. As I type this I am about 4 minutes into watching the start of my turn on a really insane run because every action is done on the fly rather than pre-calculated. This leads to weird situations like being able to draw from a deck before certain cards are added or being able to move items around in the middle of the animations being played. I also have so many products trigger on my turn that I had to remove my Bonus Insurance card because it would completely hang the game for a minute or so every time I tried playing it. I have tried adjusting the in game options to see if I could speed this up but unfortunately even with all the effects turned off, the game still has to run most animations which take time.

One quality of life change would be to include a way to auto-draw while your explosion chance is greater than 0%. Having to spam click the draw button when there is a button that automatically plays your hand just doesn't make much sense.

EDIT: The game gets a lot harder after reaching difficulty 5. So far I am still able to win with a bit of effort but it may start getting too hard for players that can't commit several hours to the game. Still a lot of fun to play, but be aware that at higher difficulties you could lose before you even really start your run.

comment_evidence.clause: Together with the visuals you get a very atmospheric and off-kilter experience that feels like what you'd get out of a bunch late teenage graveyard folks on a bit too much wine and video game enthusiasm
comment_evidence.full_review:
I love Cryptmaster. At first I thought it might be a bit too crosswordy for me, that it'd leave me in the dust so to speak. But no... it eases you into it, to such a degree that I could start plucking out the eyeballs of the hardier words with surgical ease. Well, except from those where I bruteforced the last letter because I'll be taffed up a lightpost if I know the word mellif-somethingsomething. But that comes much, much later. Cryptmaster doesn't really care to be scrabbler than thou. Most words you'll encounter are really mundane; the entire point is teasing out "what" mundane word the parser is looking for. And that is where the magic lies. Its like re-teaching yourself all the basics, and Cryptmaster is spelndid at doing that, without feeling like you're wearing a duncehat in a corner.

Its unique all the way through in regards to gameplay: get letters to spell out words, then guess the words to progress your duuds. Then you spell out words in order to wallop smegheads, or remember something from one of your characters' backstories. I played most of the game in turnbased mode, and while I appreciate that that is a massive downscaling in difficulty and not the recommended mode, I felt it suited how I interacted with the game in a ponderous, rather than action oriented fashion. Don't be afraid to play in turnbased mode. What you've got to prove anyway?

The visuals are astonishing. How each area of the game can feel distinct from one another in a black white subterranean setting speak to how unified the game's aesthetic vision is. It feels like a high-end goth webcomic thats taken some cues from old D&D artwork. The same goes for the music; a combination of cold dream-pop and darkwave synthersizer landscapes having intercorse with shoegaze guitars and heavy rock rhythmns. They even feature a little regal harpsicorde ditty. Very catchy stuff. Together with the visuals you get a very atmospheric and off-kilter experience that feels like what you'd get out of a bunch late teenage graveyard folks on a bit too much wine and video game enthusiasm.

So easy recommend. This game is great and I'm not even finished teasing out all the secrets yet. Which I of course will do in due course, just know you gotta comb the areas, as well as your own grey matter in order to accomplish some of the later game puzzles.

comment_evidence.clause: The aesthetics are quite good and make excellent use of the black & white palette reminiscent in color of  the original 1987 Shadowdark release on ancient Apple Macintosh computers
comment_evidence.full_review:
This game begs for a pun. I will avoid the temptation. 
 
It's a retro dungeon crawler that has word games and riddles at it's core. Even from the beginning such puzzles were a consistent mainstay of Dungeon Master, Wizardry and Bard's Tale. Although rather easy typing is the core combat mechanic with some very light traditional RPG tactics layered on top there is also a huge amount of puzzles. These range from simple to quite difficult especially some of the optional ones. Combat is rarely difficult and the writing is consistently facetious but can elicit a chuckle or a smile.  
 
The aesthetics are quite good and make excellent use of the black & white palette reminiscent in color of  the original 1987 Shadowdark release on ancient Apple Macintosh computers. Actual rooms are repetative but in the way old 3-D dungeon crawlers were.  
 
Special call out to the voice-work. Just excellent and really elevates the whole experience. This along with some amusing responses to answers shows a lot of care was made in the player experience. This is why I recommend this game. It's fun and interesting and doesn't overstay it's welcome.  By the time you get tired of the mechanics your probably a little over half-way done.  
 
In the end of it this is a bunch of old mechanics dressed up to hide the old bones. Reminding us that older computer games were more focused, playful, and not afraid to be a little cute and clever. If you want to be briefly amused by a few puzzles and easy laughs this is a good pick.

comment_evidence.clause: The black and white visuals do little to redeem this and perhaps even add to the repetitive look of the dungeon
comment_evidence.full_review:
[h2] It is good, just not good enough [/h2]
I get what the developers are going for and commend them for their hard work and novel idea. However, there is not much meat on this bone. For the 25 USD price point the game has not met my expectations. Combat is lacking, some mechanics are straight up bad and should be removed, and the game can soft lock you repeatedly during random encounters

[h3]The 'Wordle' part[/h3]
The setup of the game is simple. You type words to execute an action or attack. You find new actions or attacks by revealing words one at the time per character. The way the game helps you discover the words is through combat, which reveals 1 letter you choose, or through riddles, where the letters in the answer will apply to all of the characters speeding up the discovery proces.

[h3]Combat[/h3]
The combat is based on the player typing these discovered words. 
- One of the main gripes I have with combat is the cooldown mechanic. It completely removes the player's typing speed from the combat skill equation: How fast you can type only matters at the initial attacks, after that you just line up the words and hit enter after the character's cooldown expires. 
- There is also not a lot of variety in attacks between characters
- Some words (like [spoiler]salmon[/spoiler] or [spoiler]urchins[/spoiler]) do the same thing on the same character. 
- The overview of all the unlocked 'words' (i.e. attacks) mixes the important attack words with other useless 'memory' words that have no use throughout the game
- Enemies have a shield that can soft lock you (You unlock [spoiler]crack[/spoiler] early on in the game for [spoiler]jorro[/spoiler]. If the shield enemies have [spoiler]armor you need to crack[/spoiler] before being able to do damage. An enemy shield that states any of the letters that are used in the word can counter it, making it so you can't progress and just have to wait for your party to die. 
- [spoiler]The armor mechanic also makes heavy hitting attacks much less useful, as you have to remove the armor before being able to deal more damage. So knowing puppet, rattle or cackle (which are all, again, stacked on the same character) often does little[/spoiler]

[h3] Exploring [/h3]
The exploring gets old quickly. All areas start to look the same. Rocks, grass, a wooden door and rampart. It never really changes. The black and white visuals do little to redeem this and perhaps even add to the repetitive look of the dungeon. The rooms you will explore can be quite big. As a dungeon crawler it makes sense you want to explore these rooms, but the game does nothing to reward you for it. You can waste a lot of time navigating all the nooks and crannies of the map, expecting perhaps a chest or puzzle, but instead be rewarded with more black and white walls.

[h3] Puzzles and Riddles [/h3]
The riddles are great and are a nice addition to the game. The mental switch from 'Wordle Dungeon Crawler' to solving riddles is fun and feels good. Not all riddles are equal though, some are unoriginal and you've probably heard before many times whereas others are quite clever and new. The one thing they completely messed up is that not all riddles have the correct answer. 

Early on the game acknowledges this in the [spoiler]tombs[/spoiler]. The riddle [spoiler]What has an eye but cannot see[/spoiler] can be given multiple answers and the NPC will reply with [spoiler]I did not expect that particular answer but it is also correct so here is your prize[/spoiler]. You can answer [spoiler] blind, needle or storm [/spoiler] and all will be true and counted as such.

Later in the game this completely goes away. For example the riddle [spoiler] What do you have but never use, and others use all the time[/spoiler] requires the answer [spoiler]name[/spoiler], but a) [spoiler] you do use your name to introduce yourself [/spoiler] and [spoiler] In that case something akin to 'your reputation' [/spoiler] should also fit. Or [spoiler] Your phone number [/spoiler]. There are many riddles that can be given multiple answers to in this game and I was hoping, due to the core mechanic being trial and error inputting words, the game would accommodate this throughout the game.

This makes solving riddles much more frustrating and less fun. It makes it feel abitrary. It highlights the fact that the 'dungeon master' that you interact with has much more limited interactions than you'd expect at first. 

The game also has a big difficulty spike at [spoiler] Ulara castle [/spoiler] when it comes to riddles. There is one where you straight up need [spoiler] create an algebraic function and solve it [/spoiler]. It makes the pacing feel weird and the new area feel like a brick wall which I am sure will discourage a lot of players. You can have the narrator literally give you the answer after 1 or 2 tries, but for a game about solving riddles, where is the fun in that.


[h3] The story [/h3]
You are probably not buying this for the story but rather for the gameplay mechanics described above. If you mainly want a good dungeon crawler story, this is not the game for you. The characters in this story are weak and interchangeable. Your party of heroes consist of mutes. The game tells you to talk to NPCs and interact with them using action keywords like 'talk', 'use' or anything contextual. But 90% of the time you can't talk to the NPCs and the dungeon master gives you the same reply again and again. 'You will talk when I will tell you to' as you roll your eyes and move towards the next door on your map. The fun and interesting parts in the story are few and far between.

[h3] Conclusion [/h3]
The game has an insane amount of potential. It just needs a lot more polish and more thought into the design elements of the game. The gameplay loop could use a review. The combat needs a complete overhaul that caters more towards typing fast while remembering the words you unlocked, removing the cooldowns or making them much shorter will be a great start. Currently the game to me is a 4 or 5 out of 10 because of the reasons mentioned above. With some more TLC it can be a 7 or 8.

comment_evidence.full_review:
You know those ideas that sounds good on paper but not great in action? This is a prime example and it pains me to say that cause I want to like the game but it's just gimmicky and the gameplay can't support itself

Gameplay loop for me has been
- Enter combat, type HIT, ZAP, JAB, with minimal variation
- Win said combat, pick a letter and hope I can find more skills that could be useful but I don't
- Move around the map to figure out what the hell I'm supposed to do
- Get lost, forget what I was doing and search for clues cause there's no quest journal or pointers (I have ADD, bite my butt if you think every game should be like DS with zero hand holding/ quest tracker)
- Find bugs to get spelling points that I don't use cause I just do HIT ZAP JAB cause it just works
- Find a riddle and try to complete it but can't cause I'm an idiot
- Enter combat...

The art style is very nice, the voice acting is very well done but it all fall short over how the map/UI/quest design is terrible. And this to me is the biggest problem of them all: the game was more fun when I was playing on controller... a typing game, was better on controller... it says a lot about the shortcomings of this game

comment_evidence.full_review:
TL;DR: A fun and engaging game with a relatively short playtime to complete and getting 100% Steam Achievements is very easy.

[h1] Positives [/h1]
[list]
[*][b] Visuals [/b]: The graphics are very simple but pleasing to look at and interactable gameplay elements such as resources and jellyfish are both visually distinct and coloured to differ from the environment.
[*][b] Upgrades [/b]: The upgrade tree is fairly priced and the stat changes, game mechanics, resource facilities, and new currencies are handled so well that each upgrade felt like it was useful progression and not a grind.
[*][b] Game Length [/b]: This is a relatively short game that can be beaten in one sitting. It's constantly engaging and there wasn't any unnecessary padding or difficulty curve to extend playtime. It's simply select level, dive, sell loot, upgrade, repeat; with each cycle lasting a few minutes.
[*][b] Steam Achievements [/b]: You can wholly get all Steam Achievements in a single playthrough and it's very simple to do so as nearly all are tied by progression with the only one that breaks away from this being to purchase all upgrades, which at the endgame is basically pocket change.
[/list]

[h1] Negatives [/h1]
[list]
[*][b] Clipping [/b]: This is my only gripe with the game. Since both jellyfish and resources can clip into the environment, it isn't that bad as jellyfish can still be defeated and thus collected, but resources that clip into the environment can be a mood breaker having to lose progression on breaking it only for it drift away and out of range of the plasma tool. This isn't an issue late game as spawn rates will allow plasma-chain to nullify this problem, but it's quite prevalent in the early to mid-game.

Do you remember the pure joy of neopets and tamagotchi?  
 
Do you miss having those simple endearingly adorkable pets to look after, without a bunch of fussy gameplay that later creature catcher games introduced?  
 
Well here's the perfect fix at a low price, with the bonus of multiple pets being available *if* you want them.  
 
This game is too cute. The little animations some of the pets have will make you fall in love with them and feverently swear to never let them starve or get sold.  
 
Your little origami fortune teller says buy this, and the eight ball keychain agrees, and your mood ring lip gloss shows you're excited for it but trying to hide that. Swallow your "adulting" instincts down and drop the couple bucks to have this playing while you work or doom scroll. You won't regret it.

comment_evidence.clause: - When there are a bunch of animals on the farm it would be nice if we could click them and milk for coins from the menu
comment_evidence.full_review:
Oh hey! I didn't actually review this and I thought I did long ago. This is such a cute little game, a great idler, something nice to have on the bottom of the screen.

So the pros:
- The animals are, largely, cute. 
- If you have a favorite animal, you can get that animal up, through rainbow breeding, to millions of coins if you want. This means there are no animals that 'go to waste'. If you want little corgis running around and red pandas posing: you can do that. It's a lot of work... it's a LOT of hours, but there comes a point where you generate so much gold that this is easily done.
- The props are pretty nice and the automated stuff will truly automate things with only a bit of loss.
- The fish DLC is pretty nice, there are a things I'd like with that, but overall I like it. The water effect is cool where it dips where you put your mouse cursor at the top like you are dipping it in water and I like that. 
- The screen options are really nice, you can have a massively zoomed in farm or an itty-bitty farm with all your critters and props. 
- The constant collabs give some really cool creatures, they don't give a ton so they aren't broken, but even cosmetic animals can be bred higher if you want.
- The color variants are pretty nice and none of them are bad.

The things I'd like possibly looked at:
- The water stuff: I'd love more water variants. I posted in the forums but I'd love a water version the bees in the form of hermit crabs, or the broom could be snails. Things like that so we can make a real aquarium.
- Some of the props actually have use, but I'd love it if all of them did. Like maybe the Corgi jumps on the bench, or the rabbit and cat hide under it.

The biggest thing I'd like: 
- When there are a bunch of animals on the farm it would be nice if we could click them and milk for coins from the menu, or... and this is a big one: If we could have a little window in the farm where we could have the petting and clicking animations. We have the ability to turn off coin collecting so we can just pet them, but when you have a ton of animals it could be hard. I'd love to have them bigger on my screen, just a little one wandering in a window that I can click on. Think Dogz and Catz from the Windows 3.1 days. I really think this game could have a DLC just for that. Let us raise an animal and then pull that into it's own little sub window with some props, it can wander and we can pet it. In fact, as a punishment, in the pen it doesn't generate gold but can still need feeding and stuff. Imagine chilling with the Capybara just chilling while we pet it but taking up a third of our screen?  

Yeah... yeah I'd pay for that. I have, actually, as I bought Dogs and Catz many times. You have so many cute animals here that it could be fun.

There is a lot I like and very, VERY, little I don't. This isn't just a recommended game as I've actually forced it on friends by sending it to multiple of them. I kind of feel like anyone who likes animals or idlers would like it.

comment_evidence.clause: The shop menu for water-related items is a bit clunky too
comment_evidence.full_review:
Tiny Pasture is a wonderful semi-idle game that adds an adorable pixel graphic farm to the bottom of your screen.

The concept is simple: you buy animals, and they live at the bottom of your screen. Like a Tamagotchi, you need to feed them and clean up their droppings, or they’ll get sick and stop generating income. If that happens, you’ll need to buy medicine to make them happy again.

Each animal is a randomized roll for color variation and rarity. Higher rarity means more money earned. Rarities go from grey, blue, gold, red, to rainbow. You can also breed lower-tier animals together to get a higher rarity for free. Most animals have several color variations, so your pastures can be nice and colorful. You can also pet and name your animals.

There are multiple pastures to unlock, and tons of ways to customize them with backgrounds, foregrounds, and decorative items. Each one can feel unique.

That said, it does take some setup to really get going. Over time, you unlock “facilities,” functional decorations you can upgrade to automate things like feeding, cleanup, and coin collection, but getting to that point takes a bit of time.

One of my biggest gripes is that inactive pastures don’t generate income. If you want to achievement hunt or aim for rainbow-quality animals (which you can’t breed, only roll), you’ll need a lot of coins. I had to let my screen idle for hours with red-quality cows just to afford rainbow rolls. I’m used to grindy idle games, but I can see how that might frustrate some players.

The aquarium expansion was a cute addition, but also a little awkward. The fish are great, and the tanks are customizable, but the facilities don’t match the new aquatic theme. For example, underwater trees with bees are collecting coins, which breaks immersion. Also, fish can be placed in any pasture, not just tanks. The shop menu for water-related items is a bit clunky too, lumped under a single button and requiring some scrolling instead of being properly sorted.

All that said, I think it’s clear by my hours that I really enjoyed this game. Normally when I finish achievement hunting, I mark a game as done and move on, but when the water expansion dropped, I kept playing.

I’ve since moved on to another idler, but Tiny Pasture gave me so many cozy hours and lovable little critters to watch. A lot of people say it’s only worth getting on sale, but honestly? It’s less than a Starbucks coffee, and I think it’s worth full price. That’s just me, you can decide for yourself. 

I'll definitely be picking this game back up if another expansion ever drops.

comment_evidence.full_review:
Really cute! The models and animations are adorable and while it is pretty grindy most of it is just letting it run in the background after a few hours of gameplay. Only issue I have is I wish there was a better way to make early game pets meta. I know 5 stars don't have a limit but when you're trying to breed a bunny to take to late game, it's just really not worth it (I've spent hours and I haven't even reached 1k per minute. I'm on around 100k per minute usually now) I wish there was a way to buff them significantly, maybe by spending money for some kind of item or merging them with a stronger pet for a larger boost. It'd be nice to have a stupid op bunny around (balanced ofc)

Also as a small tip for early game (Please don't patch this devs getting money in early before I found this made my wrist hurt lmao) if you hold click and drag on an animal on the side of your screen (at least for me), they'll run in place and keep dropping coins. And if you do this for long enough, they'll get stuck to your cursor and keep chasing you even if you let go. You can stop this by clicking on them again. You can do other stuff on your monitor while this is happening and feed your animals without it lettin em go, good for getting out of early game easily!

And for those who wanna grind the achievements: Just continuous buy animals set to 5 star for em. I tried breeding the 4s together but I have still yet to obtain one that way, ONLY by purchasing. Then, grab 1 of every other type. You can just buy one of any rarity and keep rerolling until you get one you've yet to encyclopedia. Then, slowly breed the 5 star into every type of animal (Use the setting in the breeding menu to keep the color you haven't gotten yet or else you won't get the one you want and you'll have to wait for it to grow up. Then you should have them all! And if you're a completionist and want to keep all the types as rainbows at once, just buy the amount of rainbows you need based on how many variants there are. That seems annoying for the late game expensive pets but it gets it done fast and easy so meh.

I do however have a few small annoyances with the game after I've 100%d it, the first being that most of the grind to get all the pasture slots and just money in general require me to just- leave my computer running all night with the game on so I can get money. Other than that, there's little way to make a large amount of money needed to complete the game without wanting to rip your hair out. I feel it'd be best to be able to earn idle income based on your animals and the levels of your facilities, of course if your feeder isn't a high level it shouldn't work at least for that long, but maybe the amount of time you're allowed to stay away at once can increase the more levels you have in the feeder and broom

Another smaller gripe is the breeding times. I wish there was some kind of facility where you could lower them since, again, most of the gameplay past a certain point is just farming BILLIONS, and getting animals that make at least 1 mil+ per minute is generally the best way to do that, but it's SO tedious when you're constantly forced to breed rainbow frogs over and over taking hours for it to grow back up again just to add on a bit of progress, and don't get me started on lower tier animals that take almost the exact same amount of time to grow up but give far less money

Anyways, game good, has some issues, I've yapped too much about this, I will likely only be playing again if there's more achievements added because it's kind of tedious to be honest.

https://youtu.be/_xsDUiDxwJg

[h2]Better With Friends[/h2]
I originally played the Steam demo during a past Steam Next Fest, and honestly, it wasn’t good. There wasn’t much to the playtest. You hopped through stages that all felt the same until you hit a boss. That was basically it, it felt rusty and in need of some elbow grease.

Thankfully, a lot has changed since then. The game is wider in scope and much bigger when it comes to build diversity. That said, the core issue is still there. There isn’t a huge amount of content to play through, and the loop does become repetitive fairly quickly as all you're doing in running through the same small arenas in search of the same best in slot builds. If you don't get a good build, you have to made due with what you find and if you can't make due, you can always try again or force remove all the boring builds and enable the best builds when you can farm enough currency to unlock more of those features.

But here’s the thing. Ask yourself how repetitive a game like Path of Exile really is. Running the same builds every league, replaying the exact same story for thousands of hours, and then turning around and saying you hate repetition in Shape of Dreams feels a bit silly no?

Repetition alone isn’t the problem. It’s whether the loop is enjoyable, and that depends heavily on how and who you play it with. Playing alone, I had fun, but that's mostly because I ran into an issue on my first two runs.

[h2]Issue[/h2]
My first two runs felt oddly forced, or maybe just unusually lucky? I was playing Lizard Boy and got Arrow Storm almost immediately in both runs, followed by a stack of 20% attack speed modifiers and a bunch of on-hit effect essences. It let me completely shred bosses and entire arenas with Ricochet with very little resistance. In another run, I pulled multiple Mind Corruption spells with heavy sustain and massive shielding, where  every boss was a joke as I just stood there on hard difficulty and even nightmare difficulty with a bajillion shield while avoiding some minor mechanics. Like, it's fun, but not THAT fun. 

There are clearly a lot of ways to win, but those wins feel short-lived. You’re still fighting the same bosses, reaching the same endings, and looping through the same structure without it going anywhere interesting, the appeal is creating new skill effects based on what you get.

I haven’t unlocked Lucid Dreaming yet, but from what it does, it mostly just breaks the game’s rules to give you even more control, which only makes things feel more trivial rather than deeper.

Sound effects blur together and become extremely annoying in the later stages when multiple people are blasting their way through enemies, not a satisfying cascade of sound.


[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
This isn’t me saying the game is bad. It’s more that you’re running through the same stages, and you’ll notice that pretty quickly. The loop is simple: clear enemies, hunt for secret zones to unlock powerful statues, avoid being hunted by the hunters, claim rewards, and cosmetics, then push toward the boss with whatever builds you’ve pieced together. You can swap builds at any time, even play nothng but the same build (x4) which is nice, then you exit the dream.

It’s fun in short bursts, but the repetition sets in fast. Playing with friends or random players online can be great until they are the ones coming in with the best in slotted skills and effects carrying you through every single encounter where you're mostly dead and watching.

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]
Shape of Dreams has once again improved a lot since its demo, especially when it comes to build variety and overall scope. The gameplay is fun, and experimenting with different setups can feel rewarding, when playing alone, with friends and sometimes with strangers.

The problem is longevity. Runs blur together, bosses repeat, and progression doesn’t really evolve into anything more interesting over time. Wins come easily if the game hands you the right tools early, which makes success feel less earned and less memorable.

There’s a solid foundation here, but unless the loop expands in a more meaningful way with that cliffhanger of an ending where some dude is seen watching you leave the dream, then the game risks wearing out its welcome faster than it should.

comment_evidence.full_review:
Hack and slash for all eternity is the name of the game. The balances are interesting and the levels of added challenge give it definite replayability, though I'm personally quite fed up at the point where Limbo was unlocked - the challenge in Limbo boils down to donning up for one fight and one fight only, albeit it's divided into three stages. It's still one fight you build up for an hour a pop and then watch it all go down the drain because you didn't smack 'em up before the fires start squirting all around town. 
 
But until that point, learning the map, the builds, how each stack up and to which character - it's all fun and games. I'd say Shape of Dreams is a really nice rogue-lite experience with fancy graphics to keep your eye occupied from seeing that it is essentially just good ol' smack 'em up with the brains in between rooms instead of in the play within.

comment_evidence.clause: The idea of dreams and reality is quite good and the art and levels are designed well but a little bit more focus on interesting characters and story beats would really have helped immersion and given another hook
comment_evidence.full_review:
Shape of dreams strikes me as just being a solidly put together game. It has a clear idea of what it is wanting to achieve. The combat is satisfying and supported by a large selection of customisation both within and between the runs that give you some meaningful choices. It rewards your time well with extra characters unlocked quickly and plenty of available skills to unlock and upgrade (for reference I have all the characters unlocked whilst plenty of skill upgrading left to do after 20 hours). 
 
My main criticism of the game doesn't really affect the enjoyment but more a missed opportunity and that is the narration and lore in the game is really just a collection of rather uninteresting fluff. The idea of dreams and reality is quite good and the art and levels are designed well but a little bit more focus on interesting characters and story beats would really have helped immersion and given another hook. Not a deal breaker by any means as the rest of the game holds up well without it. 
 
In terms of customisation there is a lot to choose from and it opens up quite nicely as you progress. Each character is quite distinct and has a different playstyle that you can further customise with a nicely realised skill tree that unlocks at a good rate of knots. The skills you can select have a good number of choices and the addition of a "flexible" branch of the skill tree is a nice touch. In runs you get your "memories" or abilities that you can level up and also modify with "essences". These allow for some fun combinations and make sure runs differ significantly, I would prefer a bit of simplification on the descriptions and clearer indicator on how they affect your stats would be nice. The game is also quite generous with re-speccing mid run, you can switch things in and out easily to recycle them into the upgrade currency when you are not needing them any more. 
 
Overal a really solid title (a classic 8/10 game), particularly with a couple of friends. The game looks and sounds great, respects your time and has a lot of depth and customisation available. A little less word salad and fluff would help making builds and more charisma would boost this to a 9/10.

comment_evidence.full_review:
Super fun action-roguelike, 9/10.

- lots of build variety
- different characters with their own unique perk tree
- leveling characters and the perks is fast and uncomplicated
- combat is fun and smooth
- difficulty can be adjusted in many ways with an extra hard mode
- difficulty feels more like a skill check rather than a dps check or like a no hit run
- boss fights and their designs are for the most part uniquely designed
- map design looks beautiful and are themed uniquely
- nice feature to lock items or start with items for easy build crafting and long runs
- multiplayer is fun too, chat and emotes available
- game can be modded, so unlimited potential there

The only weakness I can think of is that maps get pretty repetitive and the enemies therefore too.

comment_evidence.clause: That ethereal visual tone is not only in keeping with the games themes of dreams but also offers something of a signature feel in a genre that can often be rather same-y as far as aesthetic is concerned
comment_evidence.full_review:
Better than I thought it would be. That statement sounds unfair and in some ways, it is. I mistook the ethereal visual tone for something closer to a deliberately childish affect, which of course could only mean the game itself would be childish. This, of course, is entirely untrue. That ethereal visual tone is not only in keeping with the games themes of dreams but also offers something of a signature feel in a genre that can often be rather same-y as far as aesthetic is concerned. In short, it’s a good game and shame on me for thinking less of it before I’d even given it a chance.

Even on the harder settings, “Shape of Dreams” (SoD) is on the easier side of action rogue-lites. That can change in a hurry, thanks to modifiers and the ability to recurse/loop your run rather than end at the final boss. Having several different levers to adjust difficulty or challenge in ways best suited to you or your mood is an absolute win. When you want to relax, you can coast; when your inner try-hard comes a-callin’, you can get your teeth kicked in. 

Another thing SoD has going for it: not only does it support co-op for up to four (4) players, but it lets people join (or rejoin) midgame. Halle-freakin’-lujah. It’s about god-d@mned time. Thank you, Lizard Smoothie.

Progression mechanics are daunting at first but relatively easy to learn, which offers its own enticement to extend replayability. Characters are distinct, in both kit and feel, which offer a way to explore the game with a varied range of abilities. Ranged classes are still strongest (and that will always be the case in these sorts of games) but most of the melee characters don’t feel overly punitive. Importantly, all of the characters I’ve played have felt responsive and (at least mostly) viable. It’s true that each character has a preference for certain kinds of builds but there’s still a good degree of freedom in how to pursue or compliment that build.

There’s some variety in level/act/chapter progression, but more would be nice. There’s good enemy variety already, but more of that would be nice, too.

The soundtrack’s not bad, either. ;-)
 
SoD gets a thumb up, scores a 7/10 on the numbers side of the house. If you’re looking for a more-than-serviceable isometric action rogue-lite with more than a dash of novelty, SoD will get you there. While it’s better than fine for single, it seems at its best in multiplayer. This means don’t dream alone, especially if you can convince [strike]one of your friends to carry you on Vesper[/strike] 2 or 3 of your friends to share the dream… the dream of victory. Recommended for: members of the Ravenswatch who want players to be able to join/abandon a run in progress; seekers of the grail who wanted something more from their time with “Sworn” ; lovers of well-crafted, co-op action rogue-lites with a distinct look and feel.

comment_evidence.clause: the protagonist's notebook containing enemy info and codes looks completely generic and clashes horribly with the rest of the game's art direction
comment_evidence.full_review:
❗ For the English version, please scroll down. ❗

Я купил Horripilant главным образом потому, что визуальный стиль и сеттинг очень напомнили мне артбуки Vermis — а Vermis, как известно, очень стильная штука. Не то чтобы меня реально интересовали айдлеры или головоломки, но я предполагал, что игра просто не будет мешать наслаждаться визуалом, атмосферой и, вероятно, даже сюжетом. Что-то типа «настраиваешь айдлер-экономику, периодически в каких-то ключевых точках решаешь адвенчурные головоломки, повторять до достижения концовки». Я ошибался.

Во-первых, айдлер тут далеко не идеальный. Да, добыча ресурсов производится в стандартном режиме "либо кликай активно, либо жди пассивно" и работает нормально. Но для любого серьезного прогресса нужно еще и отправлять героя в забеги в подземелье. Их тоже можно проводить активно, кликая по слабым местам врагов и пользуясь расходниками, либо пассивно — но нельзя автоматизировать сам момент спуска в подземелье. Вам нужно будет раз в, скажем, 15-30 минут запускать их вручную. Для айдлера какое-то слишком активное вовлечение, тем более что ничего действительно интересного в забегах нет.

Во-вторых, адвенчурная часть игры тоже сделана сомнительно. Далеко не все головоломки действительно логичны, а системы подсказок в игре нет. Сюжета тоже толком нет — вы видите набор не слишком связных сцен и образов, которые не выстраиваются ни во что цельное. Тексты написаны довольно пресно и даже вызывают легкие подозрения о том, что их писала нейросеть. Общий сюжет игры можно уместить буквально в нескольких предложениях и ничего не потерять. А раз игра — плохой айдлер и посредственная адвенчура, зачем в нее вообще играть?..

В ней, конечно, есть плюсы. Действительно классная мрачная графика с грубым дизерингом. Неплохой звуковой дизайн. Очень уместно расставленные элементы хоррора: вы несколько раз вздрогнете, но это не скример-фест, и пугалки оправданы атмосферой. Но и тут не все идеально: например, блокнот протагониста с заметками о кодах и о врагах оформлен очень дефолтно, вообще не в стиле всей остальной игры. Почему — неясно.

Кроме того, технически игра работает хорошо. Никаких серьезных багов я не заметил, системные требования весьма умеренные. Из коробки доступен русификатор — причем вполне неплохой. Кроме того, есть встроенные читы через консоль разработчика — если вас бесит айдлер-часть, можно пробежать ее буквально за час и играть просто в короткую странную адвенчуру.

Пожалуй, рекомендовать Horripilant в текущем виде я не могу почти никому. Если вам ну очень понравился визуальный стиль и вы нормально переносите сложные адвенчуры, а также готовы вручную раз за разом прокачивать снаряжение героя и отправлять его в забеги — можно попробовать, но без завышенных ожиданий. Во всех остальных случаях — лучше воздержаться. Оно того не стоит даже не в смысле цены игры, а в смысле затрат времени (если играть честно — часов двадцать у вас уйдет наверняка).

4 из 10
___

I bought Horripilant mainly because its visual style and setting strongly reminded me of the Vermis artbooks — and Vermis, as we all know, oozes style. It’s not that I’m particularly drawn to idle games or puzzles, but I figured the gameplay wouldn't get in the way of soaking up the visuals, the atmosphere, and maybe even a decent story. I expected a simple loop: optimize your idle economy, solve a few point-and-click puzzles at key milestones, and repeat until the credits roll. I was wrong.

First off, the idle mechanics leave a lot to be desired. Sure, basic resource generation follows the standard "click actively or wait patiently" formula, and that part works fine. However, making any meaningful progress requires sending your hero on dungeon runs. You can handle these actively by clicking on enemy weak spots and popping consumables, or let them play out passively — but you can't automate the actual initiation of the run. You have to manually send your character into the dungeon every 15 to 30 minutes. That requires way too much micromanagement for an idle game, especially given how tedious the runs actually are.

Secondly, the adventure side of the game is just as questionable. Many of the puzzles lack basic logic, and there is no hint system to help you out. The narrative is barely there — what you get is a disjointed series of scenes and imagery that never coalesce into a coherent story. The writing is flat and generic enough to make you wonder if it was cranked out by AI. You could summarize the entire plot in a couple of sentences without losing a single thing of value. So, if it is a bad idle game and a mediocre adventure game — why even bother playing it?

To be fair, it does have its saving graces. The dark, gritty visuals with heavy dithering look genuinely fantastic, and the sound design holds up well. The horror elements are paced nicely: it’ll catch you off guard a few times, but it doesn't devolve into a cheap jump-scare fest, and the scares feel earned by the atmosphere. Yet, even the aesthetic has its flaws. For instance, the protagonist's notebook containing enemy info and codes looks completely generic and clashes horribly with the rest of the game's art direction. Why they designed it that way — baffling.

On the technical side, the game runs smoothly. I didn't run into any major bugs, and the system requirements are very modest. On a side note, there are built-in cheats accessible via the developer console — if you detest the idle grinding, you can bypass it entirely to finish the game in about an hour, treating it purely as a short, surreal adventure.

All things considered, I can hardly recommend Horripilant in its current state to anyone. If you are absolutely head over heels for the visual style, don't mind obtuse adventure games, and have the patience to manually upgrade gear and trigger dungeon runs ad nauseam — you might give it a shot, but keep your expectations in check. In all other cases — pass on this one. It is simply not worth the investment, not so much in terms of money, but in terms of your time (a legit playthrough will easily sink around twenty hours).

4/10

comment_evidence.full_review:
Horripilant é um jogo bem anômalo. Ele pega a base viciante e matemática dos jogos incrementais e a subverte, injetando uma dose de terror psicológico e uma narrativa com começo, meio e fim. 
 
O design de Horripilant reside em como ele não se apoia apenas em progressão passiva, mas exige engajamento ativo através do pensamento espacial e lógico. 
 
O ciclo de jogabilidade é brutalmente contido no início. O fluxo de recursos é lento e intencional, forçando você a gerenciar ativamente o que tem para sobreviver aos andares iniciais da masmorra. 
 
Conforme você desce por 1000 andares, o jogo revela sua verdadeira natureza. Os itens bizarros encontrados na masmorra não são apenas para aumentar estatísticas; eles são chaves para quebra-cabeças crípticos no seu acampamento. O progresso exige que você explore, entenda as dicas deixadas no ambiente e desbloqueie novas áreas, misturando a satisfação de "ver os números subirem" com a recompensa intelectual de desvendar um adventure sombrio. 
 
A comparação com Demon's Souls é cirúrgica. Ela não vem de uma jogabilidade focada em desviar ou aparar golpes, mas da opressão palpável, do isolamento e da hostilidade do mundo. 
 
Você joga como um cavaleiro velho e sem memória em uma masmorra esquecida, com o único propósito dado por uma voz misteriosa: "Mata o teu Deus. Torna-te Digno". O estilo visual retro (com uso pesado de dithering e paletas escuras) e o design de som perturbador — desde os gemidos até o som punitivo de quando você falha em uma interação — criam um ambiente sufocante. 
 
O jogo adota mecânicas de prestige e roguelike não como meros multiplicadores de bônus, mas como uma narrativa de sacrifício. O ciclo de avançar, morrer, perder quase tudo e voltar um pouco mais forte traduz o conceito de resiliência obstinada de um soulslike para a interface de um idle game. Cada bênção recebida parece ter um fardo atrelado a ela. 
 
Assim como no Nexus de Demon's Souls, os poucos personagens que você encontra pelo acampamento são estranhos, deprimentes e falam em enigmas, aprofundando o mistério sobre o que exatamente você está tentando matar lá embaixo. 
 
Horripilant prova que até mesmo os gêneros mais casuais podem ser veículos para atmosferas densas e designs de jogo sofisticados. Ele usa as limitações do idle clicker a seu favor, transformando a lentidão natural do gênero em tensão acumulada e incerteza. 
 
E para esculhambar de vez a análise, eu diria que, tradicionalmente, desenvolvedores de jogos não são bons programadores pois, talvez e só talvez, o maior grande segredo do jogo seja descobrir que o savestate é um JSON em texto plano e você pode quebrar facilmente todas as mecânicas pensadas nesse jogo editando esse arquivo... Simples assim!

comment_evidence.clause: I feel this leans more towards Thief and Dishonored than Deus Ex or System Shock - in that there's less focus on collecting an arsenal and progressing a character and more on being creative and observant with the environment
comment_evidence.full_review:
There's always the caveat that something could go wrong by the end of Early Access, but so far this has been a very impressive outing from the first round out of the gate. And with the fundamentals being as strong as they are, it's hard for me to see Fallen Aces' potential being squandered given the talent and commitment of the devs!

The term 'Immersive Sim' has always been less of a genre and more of a sauce that various games stew in, so it's important to clarify what's on offer here. I feel this leans more towards Thief and Dishonored than Deus Ex or System Shock - in that there's less focus on collecting an arsenal and progressing a character and more on being creative and observant with the environment. There's more of an emphasis on the basic 'verbs' of the gameplay and the player's toolset, as well as how they interplay with the environment. Moment to moment it often feels like a brawler (assuming you're not stealthing), but there's a lot of versatility in how you trash enemies into the environments or use said 'trash' against them. While I do think the limited inventory is a little on the tight side, it does encourage thinking/acting spontaneously during gameplay and combat, and I'm pretty sure that's the devs' intent. For a DX analogy: You don't haul around a GEP Gun in your inventory for a chance to use it, you find the object in the environment that delivers the same result.

While the devs have said there will be no major updates until 2025, the few they've delivered after their initial release are very promising and show that they have their eyes pointed in the right direction. Here's hoping they see it through!

comment_evidence.clause: theres a thing that manages your goals and stuff in the pause menu but it never updates with stuff said so if you missed what what's-his-face says on the radio due to gunfire drowning it out or something
comment_evidence.full_review:
want to love this game but it's just too easy. played the hardest difficult and breezed through it. the ai is dumb, slow and not very good at killing you. you can walk sideways and they will completely miss all 3 bullets of their barrage, walk backwards a step and they miss their melee attack so theres no need for dodging, parry and block. its trying to be immersive sim but theres no need to use the alternative paths or stealth as i can just beat them with little resistance.

also, the game's combat just doesnt click. you can jab, hook left and right, uppercut and kick but as soon as you use any melee weapon (which will be almost all the time) almost all those alternate moves are gone and all you can do is swing it, kick or throw which isnt really much. most of those options are sh*t so the only option you need to is to swing. the missing moves dont matter though as i never found myself using them and just jabbed, backstepped and repeated when using fists. the other moves are more finicky to pull off and i cant tell if it does any more damage then just the straight jab. 

the guns make this game even more of a breeze as you can just one shot to the head with no issue. if you pick up a tommy gun which has 50 bullets, that 50 are 50 almost guaranteed kills which is pretty over-powered considering that theres usually around 80 enemies at most in a level. 

the story is pretty interesting though, love the artstyle, sound design and music. level design is ok except for having to look for keys sometimes with barely any hint like chapter 2. having "i heard something going on by the docks" as your hint to finding the key to finishing the DOCK level is pretty... stupid. theres a thing that manages your goals and stuff in the pause menu but it never updates with stuff said so if you missed what what's-his-face says on the radio due to gunfire drowning it out or something, you're doomed to wander the level with your patience wearing thinner. even with all that though, the game only lasted just a little over 4 hours. maybe it'd take a bit more with a stealth playthrough or something but the stealth isnt really advanced enough for it to be interesting to do. less tools for stealth than even a dishonered knock-out only stealth run. 

overall, i think its an ok game, maybe worth the $15 especially when the rest of the game is finished but definitely one of the weaker new blood game. not a miss but not a hit either. i'd recommend checking out gloomwood instead of this one. way better immersive sim and way more content out right now.

comment_evidence.clause: But don't worry the developers integrated their discord invitation into the main menu so you can go there and get brainwashed into bullying anyone that doesn't like this "masterpiece" of a game
comment_evidence.full_review:
Did we learn that playing offline is a thing and Steam doesn't track your time that way, right? At least for reviews, I'll have refund it otherwise. I played 35 hours, happy now?

Sorry for having trash taste but the story is just bad ( I say it with no hyperbole, no streamer's sarcasm), is monotonous, predictable and overly long with over abundance of exposition in your face, coupled with the mandatory slow walk segments. It feels completely disconnected from gameplay to the point that you feel you are watching an anime on the side while playing a somewhat decent game.

Combat is fun but monotonous, I'm all for being slow during combat but for exploration please don't make me hold a button down to sprint at what should be the default speed, did you think the Knight in Hollow Knight was slow? think again, that's your speed for the whole game, the platforming is insanely amateurish and could put you to sleep, gimmick like disappearing platforms, dark places, SLOW moving pieces that you have to sit for eons to reach the other side of the other slow moving block and then the other. The entirety of Lady Ethereal "chapter" was the most boring piece of gaming I had in years, from the narrative, to the "gameplay" to the cakewalk boss, I felt robbed, this was the HARD boss? she has 3 moves + a "surprise" one that never gets you. From there is just more of the same, same patterns, same enemies, same "deep" narrative and it's over when it feels like it should enter chapter 2 instead. Silksong really spoiled me rotten, if you wanna scratch that same itch, this ain't it, and if you want more Sekiro play Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty. 

Everything that was tried to do here was done better in Katana Zero, Blasphemous 1 (but mostly 2) Salt and Sanctuary and of course Hollow Knight franchise, nothing burger game aside from gameplay which isn't much of it.

But don't worry the developers integrated their discord invitation into the main menu so you can go there and get brainwashed into bullying anyone that doesn't like this "masterpiece" of a game, try to find critics about it on the internet, there are like 3, no game is "that" good.

comment_evidence.full_review:
After almost 80 hours of running this game I must say it was such a wild ride. I went in completely blind and I'm glad I did. The moments of awe, the moments of victory, the moment of faliure and even rage all clashed together into making this game one of my favourite experiences. 

The combat is the main focus of the game. There isn't really a feeling out there to compare to the feeling in your chest when you succesfully parry an attack and activate a talisman, slowly watching the enemy's health bar decrease. The character design, the music, the background art, it all adds to the deep and tragic story of the character you play as.

There were so many boss fights and cutscenes that made me stare in shock. I was never expecting this game to be so violent both physically and emotionally. From characters breaking down in tears making you question whether fighting them was even worth it, to straight up gore, blood and brutal death.

That is in no way me saying that the game is perfect. There were quite a few times where I felt that the game was a little unfair due to the lack of invincibility frames after taking damage (that was mainly a problem at the start of the game when I had no idea how to control my movement), It is an incredibly hard game and one thing made me feel quite bad during my first few hours of the game. The game's main game mode is Standard mode and the game's quote on quote "baby mode" is called Story mode. I found standard to be incredibly hard on my first playthrough and I felt really discouraged at the beginning because the game treats it as a standard. Like if you can't beat the ACTUAL game go ahead and switch to baby mode. After switching to Story mode though I set my modifiers to almost the same difficult as Standard by the end of the game. So you do get much better at the mechanics I just wish the game made you feel less ashamed for switching to Story mode for your first playthrough.

Second flaw I personally had was glitched and crashes. My PC is nothing more then a regular laptop so I'm sure not all people struggled with this but on accasion I had my game just crash (losing me some progress) or there'd be missing character sprites or dialog. I found it quite funny though so I really don't think it's that bad. The only thing that bothered me was when my game crashed right after beating the hardest boss and I had to fight them all over again to see the ending.

All of that aside though this is one of my top games of all time. It's a story full metroidvania filled with peak fights and amazing moments. I wish you luck with Standard mode though :) You shouldn't worry about switching to story mode I actually went back and completed the whole game in standard after finishing story mode. It is mostly a steep climb while you're learning the controls and parry timing.
